sentences.zh: }}五行傳曰：「治宮室，飾臺榭，內淫亂，犯親戚，侮父兄，則稼穡不成。

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Five Elements says: "When one governs palace halls, adorns terraces and pavilions, engages in inner licentiousness, offends against kin, and insults father and elder brothers, then the crops of grain do not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The "Tradition of the Five Elements" states: "When rulers build and adorn palaces and pavilions, indulge in inner corruption, offend their kin, and insult fathers and elder brothers, the grain harvest will fail."

sentences.zh: 」謂土失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: This means that Earth has lost its proper nature and thus become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That is, Earth abandons its proper character and calamity follows.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「思心不叡，是謂不聖。

translations.literal: It also says: "If the thinking mind is not perspicacious, this is called not sage-like."
translations.idiomatic: It further says: "When deliberation lacks clarity, this is what is meant by lack of sagacity."

sentences.zh: 厥咎瞀，厥罰恒風，厥極凶短折。

translations.literal: Its fault is blindness; its punishment is constant wind; its utmost extremity is violent early death.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is confusion; the penalty is incessant wind; the extreme is sudden, violent death.

sentences.zh: 時則有脂夜之妖，時則有華孽，時則有牛禍，時則有心腹之痾，時則有黃眚、黃祥，時則有金木水火沴土。

translations.literal: At such times there are grease-of-night demons; at such times there are flower-calamities; at such times there are ox-calamities; at such times there are heart-and-belly ailments; at such times there are yellow blights and yellow auspices; at such times metal, wood, water, and fire harm Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons come demons of the black night, calamities of flowering aberration, bovine portents, diseases of the heart and viscera, yellow harbingers of ill omen, and the imbalance of metal, wood, water, and fire assailing earth.

sentences.zh: 」班固曰：「不言『惟』而獨曰『時則有』者，非一衝氣所沴，明其異大也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "It does not say 'only' but solely says 'at such times there are' because it is not a single conflicting qi that causes the harm—their difference in magnitude is thereby made clear."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu remarked: "The text does not say 'only' but repeatedly says 'in such seasons there are' because no single clashing force accounts for the harm—the variety and scale of these portents is thereby made plain."

sentences.zh: 」華孽劉歆傳以為蠃蟲之孽，謂螟屬也。

translations.literal: Flower-calamities: in Liu Xin's tradition they are taken as calamities of soft-shelled creatures—that is, the kind to which the rice-stem borer belongs.
translations.idiomatic: As for flowering calamities, Liu Xin's tradition classifies them as calamities of shelled creatures—that is, locusts and their kind.

sentences.zh: 稼穡不成

translations.literal: Failure of grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain harvest fails:

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧時，嘗歲無水旱，苗稼豐美，而實不成，百姓以饑，闔境皆然，連歲不已。

translations.literal: In the time of Sun Hao of Wu, there were years without flood or drought; seedlings and crops were lush and beautiful, yet the grain did not ripen; the people went hungry; the whole territory was thus, year after year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao of Wu there were years without flood or drought. The fields looked lush, yet the grain never ripened. Famine spread among the people, the whole realm alike, year after year without end.

sentences.zh: 吳人以為傷露，非也。

translations.literal: The people of Wu thought it was damage from dew—not so.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu blamed damage from dew, but this was not the cause.

sentences.zh: 按劉向春秋說曰：「水旱當書，不書水旱，而曰大無麥禾者，土氣不養，稼穡不成。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's Spring and Autumn exegesis: "Floods and droughts should be recorded; when floods and droughts are not recorded but it says 'great lack of wheat and grain,' it is because the qi of Earth does not nourish—the crops do not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals explains: "Floods and droughts ought to be recorded. When the chronicle omits flood and drought yet says 'great lack of wheat and grain,' it means the qi of earth fails to nourish—the harvest does not succeed."

sentences.zh: 」此其義也。

translations.literal: This is its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sense of that passage.

sentences.zh: 晧初遷都武昌，尋還建業，又起新館，綴飾珠玉，壯麗過甚，破壞諸宮，增修苑囿，犯暑妨農，官民疲怠。

translations.literal: When Hao first moved the capital to Wuchang, then soon returned to Jianye, he also built a new palace, adorned it with pearls and jade, its splendor excessive beyond measure, destroyed the various palaces, expanded and repaired gardens and parks, offending against the summer heat and hampering agriculture, officials and people exhausted and weary.
translations.idiomatic: Hao first moved the capital to Wuchang, then soon returned to Jianye. He built a new palace hung with pearls and jade, more splendid than measure allowed, tore down the old palaces, and enlarged the parks. He pressed labor through the summer heat and hindered the harvest until officials and commoners alike were worn out.

sentences.zh: 月令，「季夏不可以興土功」。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances say, "In the last month of summer one must not undertake earthworks."
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances declare, "In the last month of summer one must not undertake earthworks."

sentences.zh: 晧皆冒之。

translations.literal: Hao violated all of these.
translations.idiomatic: Hao transgressed every one of these rules.

sentences.zh: 此治宮室飾臺榭之罰，與春秋魯莊公三築臺同應也。

translations.literal: This is the punishment for governing palace halls and adorning terraces—the same correspondence as Duke Zhuang of Lu's three constructions of a tower in the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for building palaces and adorning pavilions—the same correspondence as Duke Zhuang of Lu's three tower-building campaigns recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 班固曰：「無水旱之災，而草木百穀不熟，皆為稼穡不成。」

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "When there is no disaster of flood or drought, yet the grasses, trees, and hundred grains do not ripen, all are cases of failure of grain crops."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote: "When there is no flood or drought, yet grasses, trees, and the hundred grains fail to ripen, all count as failure of the harvest."

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和十年，三麥不登，至關西亦然。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, the three grains did not ripen; it was the same as far as Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, the three grains failed; the same held as far west as Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 自去秋至是夏，無水旱，無麥者，如劉向說也。

translations.literal: From last autumn until this summer, no flood or drought, yet those without wheat—just as Liu Xiang explained.
translations.idiomatic: From the previous autumn through this summer there was neither flood nor drought, yet wheat failed everywhere—just as Liu Xiang had explained.

sentences.zh: 又俗云，「多苗而不實為傷」，又其義也。

translations.literal: Moreover the common saying, "Many seedlings but no fruit means injury"—again its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Popular lore likewise says, "Many shoots but no grain means injury"—again the same principle.

sentences.zh: 恒風

translations.literal: Constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: Incessant wind:

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始九年十一月，大風數十日，發屋折樹；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhengshi of the Duke of Qi of Wei, great wind for several tens of days, unroofing houses and breaking trees;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhengshi under the Duke of Qi of Wei, violent winds blew for many days, tearing off roofs and snapping trees;

sentences.zh: 十二月戊子晦，尤甚，動太極東閣。

translations.literal: On the last day of the twelfth month, the wuzi day, it was especially severe, shaking the eastern gate of the Great Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: on the last day of the twelfth month, the wuzi day, the storm was especially fierce and shook the eastern gate of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王嘉平元年正月壬辰朔，西北大風，發屋折木，昏塵蔽天。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Jiaping of the Duke of Qi of Wei, the renchen day, northwest great wind, unroofing houses and breaking wood, dusk dust obscuring heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Jiaping under the Duke of Qi of Wei, a northwest gale unroofed houses, snapped trees, and filled the sky with dust so thick that day seemed like dusk.

sentences.zh: 按管輅說此為時刑，大風，執政之憂也。

translations.literal: According to Guan Luo's explanation this is temporal punishment; great wind—the worry of those who hold power.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Luo interpreted this as a seasonal penalty: great wind signals anxiety among those who hold power.

sentences.zh: 是時曹爽區瞀自專，驕僭過度，天戒數見，終不改革。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Shuang was dull and self-willed, arrogant and exceeding his bounds; heaven's warnings repeatedly appeared, yet in the end he did not reform.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao Shuang was muddled and willful, arrogant beyond measure. Heaven's warnings appeared again and again, yet he never reformed.

sentences.zh: 此思心不叡，恒風之罰也。

translations.literal: This is the punishment of unperceptive thinking mind and constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for clouded deliberation and incessant wind.

sentences.zh: 後踰旬而爽等滅。

translations.literal: More than ten days later Shuang and the others were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than ten days Shuang and his faction were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「眾逆同志，至德乃潛，厥異風。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the many rebel yet share one purpose, supreme virtue withdraws; its anomaly is wind."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When the multitude rebels yet moves as one, supreme virtue withdraws; the portent is wind."

sentences.zh: 其風也，行不解，物不長，雨小而傷。

translations.literal: As for its wind: it blows without ceasing; things do not grow; rain is slight yet harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind blows without respite; nothing flourishes; the rain is slight yet damaging.

sentences.zh: 政悖德隱，茲謂亂。

translations.literal: When government contradicts virtue and virtue is hidden, this is called disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When government defies virtue and virtue is concealed, this is called disorder.

sentences.zh: 厥風先風不雨，大風暴起，發屋折木。

translations.literal: Its wind: wind first without rain; great wind suddenly rises, unroofing houses and breaking wood.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind comes first without rain; a sudden gale rises, tearing off roofs and snapping trees.

sentences.zh: 守義不進，茲謂眊。

translations.literal: Holding to righteousness yet not advancing, this is called blindness.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to righteousness yet failing to advance, this is called blindness.

sentences.zh: 厥風與雲俱起，折五穀莖。

translations.literal: Its wind rises together with clouds, breaking the stalks of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind rises with the clouds and snaps the stalks of the five grains.

sentences.zh: 臣易上政，茲謂不順。

translations.literal: When ministers easily overturn superior government, this is called not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers readily overturn the ruler's policy, this is called insubordination.

sentences.zh: 厥風大飈發屋。

translations.literal: Its wind: great blast unroofing houses.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind is a great blast that tears houses apart.

sentences.zh: 賦斂不理，茲謂禍。

translations.literal: When levies and collections are not regulated, this is called calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When levies and collections are not properly ordered, this is called calamity.

sentences.zh: 厥風絕經紀，止即溫，溫即蟲。

translations.literal: Its wind cuts off the warp and woof; when it stops it is warm, and when warm there are insects.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind severs the warp and woof of order; when it stops, warmth follows, and with warmth come insects.

sentences.zh: 侯專封，茲謂不統。

translations.literal: When marquises monopolize enfeoffments, this is called lack of unity.
translations.idiomatic: When lords monopolize their fiefs, this is called lack of unity.

sentences.zh: 厥風疾而樹不搖，穀不成。

translations.literal: Its wind is swift yet trees do not sway; grain does not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind is swift yet the trees do not sway, and the grain fails.

sentences.zh: 辟不思道利，茲謂無澤。

translations.literal: When the ruler does not consider the Way and benefit, this is called no grace.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler gives no thought to the Way and the people's welfare, this is called want of grace.

sentences.zh: 厥風不搖木，旱無雲，傷禾。

translations.literal: Its wind does not shake trees; drought without clouds; grain is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind does not stir the trees; drought comes without clouds and the grain is ruined.

sentences.zh: 公常於利，茲謂亂。

translations.literal: When the lord is constantly bent on profit, this is called disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler is constantly bent on profit, this is called disorder.

sentences.zh: 厥風微而溫，生蟲蝗，害五穀。

translations.literal: Its wind is slight yet warm; insects and locusts are born; the five grains are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind is mild yet warm; insects and locusts breed and destroy the five grains.

sentences.zh: 棄正作淫，茲謂惑。

translations.literal: Abandoning the upright and practicing licentiousness, this is called delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning what is upright and indulging in excess, this is called delusion.

sentences.zh: 厥風溫，螟蟲起，害有益人之物。

translations.literal: Its wind is warm; borer-insects arise; things beneficial to people are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Its wind is warm; stem-borers multiply and destroy what nourishes the people.

sentences.zh: 侯不朝，茲謂叛。

translations.literal: When marquises do not attend court, this is called rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When lords fail to attend court, this is called rebellion.

sentences.zh: 厥風無恒，地變赤，雨殺人。」

translations.literal: Its wind has no constancy; the earth turns red; rain kills people."
translations.idiomatic: Its wind has no constancy; the earth turns red; rain kills people."

sentences.zh: 吳孫權太元元年八月朔，大風，江海涌溢，平地水深八尺，拔高陵樹二株，石碑磋動，吳城兩門飛落。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month of the first year of Taiyuan of Sun Quan of Wu, great wind; rivers and seas surged and overflowed; on level ground the water was eight feet deep; two trees at Gaoling were uprooted; stone tablets were ground and shaken; two gates of the Wu capital flew off.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month of the first year of Taiyuan under Sun Quan of Wu, a great gale drove the rivers and sea over their banks. On level ground the water stood eight feet deep. Two trees at Gaoling were uprooted, stone tablets were ground and shaken, and two gates of the Wu capital were torn away.

sentences.zh: 按華覈對，役繁賦重，區瞀不叡之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Hua He's response, corvée labor was heavy and taxes burdensome—the punishment of dullness and lack of perspicacity.
translations.idiomatic: Hua He explained that heavy corvée and crushing taxes were the penalty for muddled, unperceptive rule.

sentences.zh: 明年，權薨。

translations.literal: The next year Quan died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Quan died.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興元年十二月丙申，大風震電。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jianxing of Sun Liang of Wu, great wind and quaking thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, violent wind and thunder shook the land.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏遣大眾三道來攻，諸葛恪破其東興軍，二軍亦退。

translations.literal: That year Wei sent a great host by three routes to attack; Zhuge Ke defeated their Dongxing army, and the other two armies also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei sent a great army along three routes. Zhuge Ke routed the force at Dongxing, and the other two columns also withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，恪又攻新城，喪眾太半，還伏誅。

translations.literal: The next year Ke again attacked Xincheng, lost more than half his troops, returned, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ke attacked Xincheng again, lost more than half his army, returned home, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 吳孫休永安元年十一月甲午，風四轉五，復蒙霧連日。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yong'an of Sun Xiu of Wu, the wind turned four or five times, then mist covered the land for many days.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, the wind shifted four or five times, then fog blanketed the land for days on end.

sentences.zh: 是時孫綝一門五侯，權傾吳主，風霧之災，與漢五侯、丁、傅同應也。

translations.literal: At that time Sun Chen's household had five marquises; their power overawed the Wu ruler; the disaster of wind and mist corresponded to the Five Marquises of Han and Ding and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time five marquisates filled Sun Chen's clan, and their power overshadowed the Wu ruler. The calamity of wind and mist matched the Five Marquises of Han and the Ding and Fu factions.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁卯夜，又大風，發木揚沙。

translations.literal: On the night of the dingmao day of the twelfth month, again great wind, uprooting trees and raising sand.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the dingmao day in the twelfth month another gale uprooted trees and hurled sand through the air.

sentences.zh: 明日，綝誅。

translations.literal: The next day Chen was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chen was executed.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始五年五月辛卯朔，廣平大風折木。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, the xinmao day, great wind in Guangping broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, a gale in Guangping snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧元年五月，下邳、廣陵大風，壞千餘家，折樹木。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, great wind in Xiapi and Guangling destroyed more than a thousand homes and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, gales at Xiapi and Guangling destroyed more than a thousand homes and broke countless trees.

sentences.zh: 咸寧元年五月甲申，廣陵、司吾、下邳大風折木。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the fifth month of the first year of Xianning, great wind in Guangling, Siwu, and Xiapi broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the fifth month of the first year of Xianning, gales at Guangling, Siwu, and Xiapi snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 咸寧三年八月，河間大風折木。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianning, great wind in Hejian broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Xianning, a gale in Hejian broke trees.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年五月，濟南大風，折木傷麥。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, great wind in Jinan broke trees and harmed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, a gale in Jinan snapped trees and damaged the wheat.

sentences.zh: 太康二年六月，高平大風折木，發壞邸閣四十餘區。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Taikang, great wind in Gaoping broke trees and unroofed and destroyed more than forty lodging compounds.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Taikang, a gale in Gaoping broke trees and tore the roofs from more than forty lodging compounds.

sentences.zh: 太康八年六月，郡國八大風。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Taikang, eight commanderies and kingdoms had great wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year of Taikang, eight commanderies and kingdoms reported great gales.

sentences.zh: 太康九年正月，京都風雹，發屋拔木。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Taikang, wind and hail in the capital unroofed houses and uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year of Taikang, wind and hail in the capital tore off roofs and uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 後二年，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: Two years later the imperial carriage rested at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康四年六月，大風雨拔樹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, great wind and rain uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, wind and rain uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 元康五年四月庚寅夜，暴風，城東渠波浪；

translations.literal: On the night of the gengyin day of the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, sudden wind; waves in the eastern moat of the city;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the gengyin day in the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, a sudden gale whipped waves through the eastern moat;

sentences.zh: 七月，下邳大風，壞廬舍；

translations.literal: In the seventh month, great wind in Xiapi destroyed cottages;
translations.idiomatic: in the seventh month a gale at Xiapi wrecked cottages;

sentences.zh: 九月，雁門、新興、太原、上黨災風傷稼。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, calamitous wind in Yanmen, Xinxing, Taiyuan, and Shangdang harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month destructive winds in Yanmen, Xinxing, Taiyuan, and Shangdang damaged the harvest.

sentences.zh: 明年，氐、羌反叛，大兵西討。

translations.literal: The next year the Di and Qiang rebelled; a great army marched west to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Di and Qiang rebelled, and a great army marched west to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 元康九年六月，飈風吹賈謐朝服飛數百丈。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, a whirlwind blew Jia Mi's court robes flying several hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, a whirlwind snatched Jia Mi's court robes and carried them hundreds of paces through the air.

sentences.zh: 明年，謐誅。

translations.literal: The next year Mi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Mi was executed.

sentences.zh: 元康九年十一月甲子朔，京都連大風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yuankang, the jiazi day, the capital had successive great winds, unroofing houses and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yuankang, successive gales in the capital tore off roofs and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 十二月，太子廢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the heir apparent was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the crown prince was deposed.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年二月，大風拔木。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yongkang of Emperor Hui of Jin, great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Hui of Jin, a great gale uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 三月，愍懷被害。

translations.literal: In the third month Minhuai was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Crown Prince Minhuai was murdered.

sentences.zh: 己卯，喪柩發許還洛，是日，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。

translations.literal: On the jimao day the funeral bier set out from Xu to return to Luoyang; that day, great wind, thunder, and lightning; curtains and canopies flew apart and split.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day the funeral procession left Xu for Luoyang. That same day wind, thunder, and lightning tore the mourning canopies from their frames.

sentences.zh: 永康元年四月，張華第舍飈風折木，飛繒軸六七。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongkang, a whirlwind at Zhang Hua's residence broke trees and sent six or seven silk bolts flying.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongkang, a whirlwind at Zhang Hua's house snapped trees and sent six or seven bolts of silk flying through the air.

sentences.zh: 是月，華遇害。

translations.literal: That month Hua was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Hua was murdered.

sentences.zh: 永康元年十一月戊午朔，大風從西北來，折木飛石。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yongkang, the wuwu day, great wind came from the northwest, breaking trees and hurling stones.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yongkang, a northwest gale snapped trees and hurled stones through the air.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，趙王倫篡位。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the Prince of Zhao usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the Prince of Zhao seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永興元年正月癸酉，趙王倫祠太廟，災風暴起，塵沙四合。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the first month of the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Zhao sacrificed at the Grand Temple; calamitous wind suddenly arose and dust and sand closed in from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the first month of the first year of Yongxing under Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Zhao offered sacrifice at the Grand Ancestral Temple. A calamitous gale sprang up and dust and sand closed in from every side.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，倫伏辜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year Lun suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year Lun was executed.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌元年七月丙寅，大風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the seventh month of the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, great wind uprooted trees and all roof tiles flew off.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the seventh month of the first year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan of Jin, a gale uprooted trees and sent roof tiles flying.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年八月，暴風壞屋，拔御道柳樹百餘株。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongchang, sudden wind destroyed houses and uprooted more than a hundred willow trees along the imperial roadway.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongchang, a sudden gale wrecked houses and uprooted more than a hundred willows along the imperial roadway.

sentences.zh: 其風縱橫無常，若風自八方來者。

translations.literal: Its wind crossed and ran without constancy, as if wind came from the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: The wind shifted without pattern, as though gales were striking from all eight directions at once.

sentences.zh: 十一月，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial carriage rested at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康四年三月壬辰，成都大風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the third month of the fourth year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, great wind in Chengdu unroofed houses and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the third month of the fourth year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, a gale at Chengdu tore off roofs and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 四月，李壽襲殺李期。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Li Shou attacked and killed Li Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Shou attacked and killed Li Qi.

sentences.zh: 晉康帝建元元年七月庚申，晉陵、吳郡災風。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the seventh month of the first year of Jianyuan of Emperor Kang of Jin, calamitous wind in Jinling and Wu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the seventh month of the first year of Jianyuan under Emperor Kang of Jin, destructive winds struck Jinling and Wu commanderies.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝升平元年八月丁未，策立皇后何氏。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the eighth month of the first year of Shengping of Emperor Mu of Jin, the Lady He was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the eighth month of the first year of Shengping under Emperor Mu of Jin, Lady He was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 是日疾風。

translations.literal: That day there was violent wind.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a violent gale blew.

sentences.zh: 升平五年正月戊戌朔，疾風。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fifth year of Shengping, the wuxu day, violent wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the fifth year of Shengping, a violent gale blew.

sentences.zh: 晉海西公太和六年二月，大風迅急。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Taihe of the Duke of Haixi of Jin, great wind, swift and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Taihe under the Duke of Haixi of Jin, fierce gales blew.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝寧康元年三月戊申朔，暴風迅起，從丑上來，須臾轉從子上來，飛沙揚礫。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month of the first year of Ningkang of Emperor Xiao Wu of Jin, the wushen day, sudden wind rose swiftly, coming from the direction of chou, then in a moment turning to come from the direction of zi, flying sand and raising gravel.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month of the first year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a sudden gale sprang up from the northeast, then in a moment shifted to the north, hurling sand and gravel through the air.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元元年二月乙丑朔，暴風折木。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month of the first year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiao Wu of Jin, the yichou day, sudden wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month of the first year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a sudden gale snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 太元二年閏三月甲子朔，暴風疾雨俱至，發屋折木。

translations.literal: On the first day of the intercalary third month of the second year of Taiyuan, the jiazi day, sudden wind and swift rain both arrived, unroofing houses and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the intercalary third month of the second year of Taiyuan, sudden wind and driving rain together tore off roofs and broke trees.

sentences.zh: 太元二年六月，長安大風拔苻堅宮中樹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Taiyuan, great wind in Chang'an uprooted the trees in Fu Jian's palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Taiyuan, a gale at Chang'an uprooted the trees in Fu Jian's palace.

sentences.zh: 其後堅再南伐，身戮國亡。

translations.literal: Afterward Jian again campaigned south; he was slain and his state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jian marched south again, was killed in battle, and his kingdom fell.

sentences.zh: 太元四年八月乙未，暴風。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day of the eighth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan, sudden wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the eighth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan, a sudden gale blew.

sentences.zh: 太元十二年正月壬子夜，暴風。

translations.literal: On the night of the renzi day of the first month of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, sudden wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the renzi day in the first month of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, a sudden gale blew.

sentences.zh: 太元十二年七月甲辰，大風拔木。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the seventh month of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the seventh month of the twelfth year of Taiyuan, a great gale uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 太元十七年六月乙卯，大風折木。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Taiyuan, great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day of the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Taiyuan, a great gale snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興二年二月甲辰，大風雨，大航門屋瓦飛落。

translations.literal: On the jiachen day of the second month of the second year of Yuanxing of Emperor An of Jin, great wind and rain; roof tiles of the Dahang Gate flew off.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the second month of the second year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin, wind and rain tore the roof tiles from the Dahang Gate.

sentences.zh: 明年，桓玄篡位，由此門入。

translations.literal: The next year Huan Xuan usurped the throne, entering by this gate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Huan Xuan seized the throne and entered the city through that same gate.

sentences.zh: 元興三年正月，桓玄遊大航南，飄風飛其䡟輗蓋。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Yuanxing, Huan Xuan toured south of Dahang; a drifting wind blew away his carriage canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Yuanxing, as Huan Xuan toured south of the Dahang crossing, a gust snatched away his carriage canopy.

sentences.zh: 三月，玄敗。

translations.literal: In the third month Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xuan was defeated.

sentences.zh: 元興三年五月，江陵大風折木。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanxing, great wind in Jiangling broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Yuanxing, a gale at Jiangling snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 是月，桓玄敗於崢嶸洲，身亦屠裂。

translations.literal: That month Huan Xuan was defeated at Zhengrong Isle; his body was also hacked apart.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Huan Xuan was defeated at Zhengrong Isle and his body was hacked to pieces.

sentences.zh: 元興三年十一月丁酉，大風，江陵多死者。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the eleventh month of the third year of Yuanxing, great wind; many died in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the eleventh month of the third year of Yuanxing, a great gale killed many people at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙四年十一月辛卯朔，西北疾風起。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, the xinmao day, a swift northwest wind arose.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, a fierce northwest gale sprang up.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年閏十月丁亥，大風發屋。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the intercalary tenth month of the fifth year of Yixi, great wind unroofed houses.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the intercalary tenth month of the fifth year of Yixi, a gale tore the roofs from houses.

sentences.zh: 明年，盧循至蔡洲。

translations.literal: The next year Lu Xun reached Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Lu Xun reached Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年五月壬申，大風拔北郊樹，樹幾百年也。

translations.literal: On the renshen day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Yixi, great wind uprooted the trees of the northern suburb—trees nearly several hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Yixi, a gale uprooted the trees of the northern suburb, some nearly three centuries old.

sentences.zh: 琅邪、揚州二射堂倒壞。

translations.literal: The two archery halls of Langye and Yangzhou collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The archery halls at Langye and Yangzhou collapsed.

sentences.zh: 是日，盧循大艦漂沒。

translations.literal: That day Lu Xun's great ships were swept away and sunk.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Lu Xun's great warships were swept away and sunk.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，又風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, wind again, unroofing houses and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day another gale tore off roofs and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 是冬，王師南討。

translations.literal: That winter the imperial army marched south to punish.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the imperial army marched south in campaign.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年四月己丑朔，大風拔木。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month of the tenth year of Yixi, the jichou day, great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month of the tenth year of Yixi, a great gale uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年六月辛亥，大風拔木。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day of the sixth month of the tenth year of Yixi, great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the sixth month of the tenth year of Yixi, a great gale uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 明年，西討司馬休之。

translations.literal: The next year a western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court launched a western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 宋少帝景平二年正月癸亥朔旦，暴風發殿庭，會席翻揚數十丈。

translations.literal: At dawn on the first day of the first month of the second year of Jingping of the Lesser Emperor of Song, the guihai day, sudden wind arose in the palace courtyard; meeting mats were turned and lifted several tens of zhang.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the first day of the first month of the second year of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor of Song, a sudden gale swept the palace courtyard and sent the meeting mats flying dozens of paces through the air.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝廢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the emperor was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor was deposed.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉二十六年二月庚申，壽陽驟雨，有回風雲霧，廣三十許步，從南來，至城西回散滅。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the second month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen, sudden rain at Shouyang; there was a whirling wind with clouds and mist about thirty paces wide, coming from the south, reaching the west of the city then turning back, scattering and vanishing.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the second month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, a sudden storm struck Shouyang. A whirlwind wrapped in cloud and mist, some thirty paces across, came from the south, reached the west side of the city, then wheeled about and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 當其衝者，室屋樹木摧倒。

translations.literal: Whatever lay in its path—houses, rooms, trees—was smashed and overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever lay in its path—houses, trees, and all—was smashed flat.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年三月，大風，拔木飛瓦。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, great wind uprooted trees and sent roof tiles flying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, a great gale uprooted trees and hurled roof tiles through the air.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年正月，大風拔木，雨凍殺牛馬，雷電晦冥。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, great wind uprooted trees; rain froze and killed cattle and horses; thunder, lightning, and darkness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, a gale uprooted trees, freezing rain killed cattle and horses, and thunder and lightning filled a darkened sky.

sentences.zh: 二月，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: In the second month the imperial carriage rested at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明七年，風吹初寧陵隧口左標折。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming of Emperor Xiao Wu, wind blew and broke the left marker at the mouth of the Chuning Mausoleum tunnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, wind snapped the left marker at the mouth of the Chuning Mausoleum tunnel.

sentences.zh: 鍾山通天臺新成，飛倒，散落山澗。

translations.literal: The newly completed Tongtian Terrace on Zhong Mountain was blown over, scattered into mountain streams.
translations.idiomatic: The newly completed Tongtian Terrace on Mount Zhong was blown over and its timbers scattered into the mountain ravines.

sentences.zh: 明年閏五月，帝崩。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the next year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the following year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝永光元年正月乙未朔，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Yongguang of the Deposed Former Emperor, the yiwei day, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Yongguang under the Deposed Former Emperor, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年三月丙申，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the third month of the second year of Taishi of Emperor Ming, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the third month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年四月甲子，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the fourth month of the second year of Taishi, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the fourth month of the second year of Taishi, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年五月丁未，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年五月己酉，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiyou day of the fifth month of the second year of Taishi, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年九月乙巳，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the ninth month of the second year of Taishi, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day of the ninth month of the second year of Taishi, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年七月甲子，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the seventh month of the second year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Later Emperor, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the seventh month of the second year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Later Emperor, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年三月丁卯，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the third month of the third year of Yuanhui, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day of the third month of the third year of Yuanhui, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年六月甲戌，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the sixth month of the third year of Yuanhui, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the sixth month of the third year of Yuanhui, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年十一月辛卯，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanhui, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yuanhui, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 元徽五年三月庚寅，京邑大風，發屋折木。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the third month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, great wind in the capital, unroofing houses and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the third month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, a great gale in the capital tore off roofs and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 元徽五年六月甲寅，京邑大風。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, great wind in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, a great gale struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 夜妖

translations.literal: Night demons.
translations.idiomatic: Demons of the black night:

sentences.zh: 魏高貴鄉公正元二年閏正月戊戌，大風晦暝，行者皆頓伏。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the intercalary first month of the second year of Zhengyuan of the Noble Township Duke of Wei, great wind with darkness at dusk; travelers all prostrated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the intercalary first month of the second year of Zhengyuan under the Noble Township Duke of Wei, a great wind brought darkness at midday, and travelers fell prostrate where they stood.

sentences.zh: 近夜妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates night demons.
translations.idiomatic: This approached a demon of the black night.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「正晝而暝，陰為陽，臣制君也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: "When at high noon it grows dark, yin dominates yang—ministers control the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang wrote: "When noon turns to darkness, yin overmasters yang—ministers control the ruler."

sentences.zh: 」時晉景王討毋丘儉，是日始發。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin Prince of Jing attacked Wuqiu Jian; that day he first set out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jin Prince of Jing marched against Wuqiu Jian, and that was the day his army first set out.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝景元三年十月，京都大震，晝晦。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jingyuan of Emperor Yuan of Wei, the capital had a great quake; day turned dark.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Jingyuan under Emperor Yuan of Wei, the capital was shaken by a great earthquake and noon turned dark.

sentences.zh: 此夜妖也。

translations.literal: This was night demons.
translations.idiomatic: This was a demon of the black night.

sentences.zh: 班固曰：「夜妖者，雲風並起而杳冥，故與常風同象也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "Night demons are when clouds and wind rise together into deep gloom, and therefore share the same portent as ordinary wind."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu explained: "Demons of the black night arise when cloud and wind rise together into deep gloom, and therefore share the same portent as ordinary wind."

sentences.zh: 」劉向春秋說云：「天戒若曰，勿使大夫世官，將令專事，冥晦。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Spring and Autumn exegesis says: "Heaven's warning seems to say: Do not let great officers hold hereditary office; soon they will monopolize affairs and bring darkness."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "Heaven's warning seems to say: Do not let great officers hold hereditary office, or they will soon monopolize affairs and bring darkness."

sentences.zh: 明年，魯季友卒，果世官而公室卑矣。

translations.literal: The next year Ji You of Lu died; indeed hereditary office followed and the ducal house was humbled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Ji You of Lu died, and hereditary office did follow until the ducal house was humbled.

sentences.zh: 」魏見此妖，晉有天下之應也。

translations.literal: When Wei saw this demon, it was the correspondence of Jin's possession of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei saw this portent, it foreshadowed Jin's possession of the realm.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十三年十二月乙未，大風晦暝。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiao Wu of Jin, great wind with darkness at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, a great wind brought darkness at midday.

sentences.zh: 其後帝崩，而諸侯違命，干戈內侮，權奪於元顯，禍成於桓玄。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor died; feudal lords defied orders; weapons turned inward in insult; power was seized by Yuan Xian; calamity was completed by Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor died, the feudal lords defied the throne, civil war broke out within the realm, power passed to Yuan Xian, and disaster culminated with Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 是其應也。

translations.literal: This was its correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: This was the correspondence.

sentences.zh: 蠃蟲之孽

translations.literal: Calamities of soft-shelled creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities of shelled creatures:

sentences.zh: 晉孝武咸寧元年七月，郡國螟；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xianning of Emperor Xiao Wu of Jin, commanderies and kingdoms had rice-stem borers;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xianning under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, commanderies and kingdoms reported rice-stem borers;

sentences.zh: 九月，青州又螟。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Qing province again had borers.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month Qing province was struck again.

sentences.zh: 咸寧元年七月，郡國有青蟲食禾稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Xianning, commanderies and kingdoms had green insects eating grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Xianning, green insects devoured the grain crops in many commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 咸寧四年，司、冀、兗、豫、荊、揚郡國皆螟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning, the commanderies and kingdoms of Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang all had borers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianning, borers ravaged the commanderies and kingdoms of Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康四年，會稽彭蜞及蟹皆化為鼠，甚眾，覆野，大食稻為災。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, at Kuaiji mud crabs and true crabs all transformed into rats, very numerous, covering the wilds, greatly eating rice and becoming a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, at Kuaiji mud crabs and river crabs all turned into rats in vast numbers that covered the countryside and devoured the rice crop.

sentences.zh: 太康九年八月，郡國二十四螟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year of Taikang, twenty-four commanderies and kingdoms had borers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year of Taikang, twenty-four commanderies and kingdoms reported borers.

sentences.zh: 螟說與蝗同。

translations.literal: The explanation of borers is the same as locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Borers are interpreted the same way as locusts.

sentences.zh: 是時帝聽讒訴。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor listened to slanderous accusations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor heeded slanderous accusations.

sentences.zh: 太康九年九月，蟲傷稼。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year of Taikang, insects harmed the crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year of Taikang, insects damaged the harvest.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康二年九月，帶方、含資、提奚、南新、長岑、海冥、列口蟲食禾葉蕩盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, Daifang, Hanzai, Tixi, Nanxin, Changcen, Haiming, and Liekou—insects ate the grain leaves until none remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, insects at Daifang, Hanzai, Tixi, Nanxin, Changcen, Haiming, and Liekou devoured the grain leaves until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧元年七月，梁、益、涼三州螟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongning of Emperor Hui of Jin, the three provinces of Liang, Yi, and Liang had borers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongning under Emperor Hui of Jin, borers struck the three provinces of Liang, Yi, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 是時齊王冏秉政。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi, Min, held power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qi, Sima Min, held the government.

sentences.zh: 貪苛之應也。

translations.literal: This was the correspondence of greed and harshness.
translations.idiomatic: This was the correspondence of greed and harsh rule.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年十月，南安、巴西、江陽、太原、新興、北海青蟲食禾葉，甚者十傷五六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning, Nan'an, Baxi, Jiangyang, Taiyuan, Xinxing, and Beihai—green insects ate grain leaves; in severe cases five or six tenths were harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning, green insects at Nan'an, Baxi, Jiangyang, Taiyuan, Xinxing, and Beihai devoured the grain leaves, destroying as much as half the crop in the worst cases.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年十二月，郡國八螟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yongning, eight commanderies and kingdoms had borers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yongning, eight commanderies and kingdoms reported borers.

sentences.zh: 牛禍

translations.literal: Bovine calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Bovine portents:

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康九年，幽州塞北有死牛頭語。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, north of the frontier in You province a dead ox's head spoke.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, beyond the northern frontier in You province the head of a dead ox spoke.

sentences.zh: 近牛禍也。

translations.literal: This approximates bovine calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This approached a bovine portent.

sentences.zh: 是時帝多疾病，身以後事為念，而託付不以至公，思心瞀亂之應也。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had many illnesses; personally he was preoccupied with affairs after death, yet his entrustments were not utterly fair—this was the correspondence of a thinking mind confused and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was often ill and brooded over the succession, yet entrusted power without full impartiality—the correspondence of a clouded, troubled mind.

sentences.zh: 師曠曰：「怨讟動於民，則有非言之物而言。

translations.literal: Shi Kuang said: "When resentment and slander stir among the people, then things that do not speak come to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kuang said: "When resentment and slander stir among the people, things that ought not to speak begin to speak."

sentences.zh: 」又其義也。

translations.literal: Again its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the same principle applies.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安中，江夏張騁所乘牛言曰：「天下方亂，乘我何之！

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era of Emperor Hui of Jin, the ox ridden by Zhang Cheng of Jiangxia said: "The realm is now in turmoil—where do you ride me to go!"
translations.idiomatic: During the Tai'an era under Emperor Hui of Jin, the ox ridden by Zhang Cheng of Jiangxia said, "The realm is in turmoil—where do you think you are taking me?"

sentences.zh: 」騁懼而還，犬又言曰：「歸何蚤也。

translations.literal: Cheng was afraid and returned; a dog also said: "Why return so early?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng turned back in fear, and a dog then said, "Why return so soon?"

sentences.zh: 」尋後牛又人立而行。

translations.literal: Soon after the ox again stood upright like a man and walked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the ox stood upright like a man and walked.

sentences.zh: 騁使善卜者卦之。

translations.literal: Cheng had a skilled diviner cast the hexagrams for it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had a skilled diviner cast the hexagrams.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「天下將有兵亂，為禍非止一家。

translations.literal: He said: "The realm will have military turmoil; the calamity will not stop at one household."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said, "War will soon convulse the realm, and the calamity will not spare a single household."

sentences.zh: 」其年張昌反，先略江夏，騁為將帥。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Chang rebelled, first overrunning Jiangxia; Cheng served as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Chang rebelled, first overrunning Jiangxia, and Cheng served as one of his commanders.

sentences.zh: 於是五州殘亂，騁亦族滅。

translations.literal: Thereupon five provinces were ravaged in disorder; Cheng too was exterminated to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Five provinces were laid waste, and Cheng's entire clan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 京房易妖曰：「牛能言，如其言占吉凶。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Changes omens say: "When an ox can speak, take its words to divine fortune or misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's omens in the Changes say: "When an ox speaks, take its words as an omen of fortune or disaster."

sentences.zh: 」易萌氣樞曰：「人君不好士，走馬被文繡，犬狼食人食，則有六畜祅言。

translations.literal: The Changes' Sprouting Qi Pivot says: "When the ruler does not cherish scholars, racing horses are draped in brocade, dogs and wolves eat human food—then the six domestic animals speak as demons."
translations.idiomatic: The Sprouting Qi Pivot of the Changes says: "When the ruler does not cherish scholars, when racing horses are draped in brocade and dogs and wolves eat human food, the six domestic animals speak as portents."

sentences.zh: 」時天子諸侯不以惠下為務，又其應也。

translations.literal: At that time Son of Heaven and feudal lords did not make benefiting those below their task—again its correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time emperors and lords did not make the welfare of their subjects their concern—again the correspondence.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建武元年，曲阿門牛生犢，一體兩頭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu of Emperor Min of Jin, at the Qu'e Gate an ox gave birth to a calf, one body with two heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Min of Jin, at the Qu'e Gate an ox bore a calf with one body and two heads.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興元年，武昌太守王諒牛生子，兩頭八足兩尾共一腹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan, the ox of Wang Liang, governor of Wuchang, gave birth—two heads, eight legs, two tails sharing one belly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, the ox of Wang Liang, governor of Wuchang, bore a calf with two heads, eight legs, and two tails sharing one belly.

sentences.zh: 三年後死。

translations.literal: Three years later it died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the calf died.

sentences.zh: 又有牛生一足三尾，皆生而死。

translations.literal: There was also an ox that bore one with one leg and three tails—all born and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Another ox bore a calf with one leg and three tails; each was born alive and soon died.

sentences.zh: 按司馬彪說，兩頭者，政在私門，上下無別之象也。

translations.literal: According to Sima Biao's explanation, two heads mean government lies in private gates—the image of no distinction between above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao explained that two heads signify government lodged in private hands—the image of no distinction between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「足多者，所任邪也。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When legs are many, those appointed are wicked."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When legs are many, those appointed are wicked."

sentences.zh: 足少者，下不勝任也。

translations.literal: When legs are few, those below cannot bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: When legs are few, those below cannot bear their duties.

sentences.zh: 」其後皆有此應。

translations.literal: Afterward all had this correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward each case found its correspondence.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興四年十二月，郊牛死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, the suburban sacrificial ox died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, the suburban sacrificial ox died.

sentences.zh: 按劉向說春秋郊牛死曰，宣公區瞀昏亂，故天不饗其祀。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's exegesis of the Spring and Autumn on the death of the suburban sacrificial ox: Duke Xuan was muddled and confused in disorder, so Heaven did not accept his sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's commentary on the Spring and Autumn explains that when the suburban sacrificial ox died, it meant Duke Xuan was blind with confusion and disorder, and Heaven refused his offerings.

sentences.zh: 元帝中興之業，實王導之謀也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's enterprise of restoration was in truth Wang Dao's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration under Emperor Yuan was in truth Wang Dao's doing.

sentences.zh: 劉隗探會主意，以得親幸，導見疏外。

translations.literal: Liu Wei probed the emperor's intent to gain intimate favor; Dao was seen as distant and excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei divined the emperor's mind to win intimate favor, while Wang Dao was kept at a distance and pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 此區瞀不叡之禍也。

translations.literal: This was the calamity of muddledness lacking perspicacity.
translations.idiomatic: This was the calamity of clouded, unperceptive rule.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和二年五月，護軍牛生犢，兩頭六足。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, the Guard Army ox bore a calf with two heads and six legs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, an ox of the Guard Army bore a calf with two heads and six legs.

sentences.zh: 是冬，蘇峻作亂。

translations.literal: That winter Su Jun rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Su Jun rebelled.

sentences.zh: 咸和七年，九德民袁榮家牛產犢，兩頭八足二尾共身。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianhe, Yuan Rong of Jiude had an ox bear a calf with two heads, eight legs, and two tails sharing one body.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianhe, Yuan Rong of Jiude had an ox bear a calf with two heads, eight legs, and two tails on one body.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳：「殺無罪，則牛生妖。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes: "When the innocent are killed, oxen bear omens."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When the innocent are slain, oxen bear portents."

sentences.zh: 桓玄之國在荊州，詣刺史殷仲堪，行至鶴穴，逢一老公，驅青牛，形色瓌異。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan's domain was in Jingzhou, he went to call on the inspector Yin Zhongkan; reaching He Cave he met an old man driving a blue ox, form and appearance strange and wondrous.
translations.idiomatic: While Huan Xuan held Jingzhou, he went to visit the inspector Yin Zhongkan. At He Cave he met an old man driving a blue ox of strange and wondrous appearance.

sentences.zh: 桓玄即以所乘牛易取。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan immediately traded the ox he was riding to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan at once traded away the ox he had been riding to take it.

sentences.zh: 乘至零陵涇溪，駿駛非常，因息駕飲牛。

translations.literal: Riding to Jing Stream in Lingling, its gallop was extraordinary; he therefore halted the carriage to water the ox.
translations.idiomatic: He rode it to Jing Stream in Lingling. Its pace was extraordinary, so he halted to water the ox.

sentences.zh: 牛徑入江水不出。

translations.literal: The ox went straight into the river water and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The ox went straight into the river and did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 玄遣人覘守，經日無所見。

translations.literal: Xuan sent men to watch; after a full day nothing was seen.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent men to keep watch, but after a full day they saw nothing.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉三年，司徒徐羨之大兒喬之行欲入廣莫門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the great son Qiao of Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi was about to enter the Guangmo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, Qiao, eldest son of Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, was riding out to enter the Guangmo Gate.

sentences.zh: 牛徑將入廷尉寺，左右禁捉不能禁。

translations.literal: The ox went straight as if to enter the Court of Prisoners; attendants forbade and seized but could not restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: The ox headed straight for the Court of Prisoners. Attendants tried to seize and hold it but could not.

sentences.zh: 入方得出。

translations.literal: Only after entering did they get it out.
translations.idiomatic: Only after it had entered were they able to lead it out.

sentences.zh: 明日被收。

translations.literal: The next day he was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was arrested.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，晉陵送牛，角生右脅，長八尺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, Jinyang sent an ox with horns growing from the right flank, eight feet long.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, Jinyang presented an ox with horns growing from its right flank, eight feet long.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，東宮為禍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, the Eastern Palace met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, calamity struck the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明三年，廣州刺史費淹獻三角水牛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, Fei Yan, governor of Guangzhou, presented a three-horned water buffalo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, Fei Yan, governor of Guangzhou, presented a three-horned water buffalo.

sentences.zh: 黃眚黃祥

translations.literal: Yellow blights and yellow omens.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow blights and yellow omens:

sentences.zh: 蜀劉備章武二年，東伐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhangwu, Liu Bei of Shu went east to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhangwu, Liu Bei of Shu marched east to attack.

sentences.zh: 二月，自秭歸進屯夷道。

translations.literal: In the second month, from Zigui he advanced and encamped at Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he advanced from Zigui and encamped at Yidao.

sentences.zh: 六月，秭歸有黃氣見，長十餘里，廣數十丈。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, at Zigui yellow vapors appeared, more than ten li long and several tens of zhang wide.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month yellow vapors appeared at Zigui, more than ten li long and several tens of zhang across.

sentences.zh: 後踰旬，備為陸議所破。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, Bei was defeated by Lu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than ten days later, Bei was defeated by Lu Yi.

sentences.zh: 近黃祥也。

translations.literal: This approximated yellow omen.
translations.idiomatic: This approached a yellow portent.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始中，中山王周南為襄邑長。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era of the Prince of Qi of Wei, Wang Zhounan of Zhongshan was magistrate of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era under the Prince of Qi of Wei, Wang Zhounan of Zhongshan served as magistrate of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 有鼠從穴出，語曰：「王周南，爾以某日死。

translations.literal: A rat came from its hole and said: "Wang Zhounan, you will die on such-and-such a day.
translations.idiomatic: A rat emerged from its hole and said, "Wang Zhounan, you are to die on such-and-such a day.

sentences.zh: 」南不應。

translations.literal: Nan did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhounan did not answer.

sentences.zh: 鼠還穴。

translations.literal: The rat returned to the hole.
translations.idiomatic: The rat went back into its hole.

sentences.zh: 後至期，更冠幘皁衣出，語曰：「周南，汝日中當死。

translations.literal: Later when the date arrived, it again came out wearing cap and black garb and said: "Zhounan, at midday you will die.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, it emerged again wearing a cap and black robes and said, "Zhounan, at midday you will die.

sentences.zh: 」又不應。

translations.literal: Again he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Again he did not answer.

sentences.zh: 鼠復入，斯須更出，語如向日。

translations.literal: The rat again entered; in a moment it came out again, speaking as on the previous day.
translations.idiomatic: The rat went back in, then shortly came out again and spoke as before.

sentences.zh: 適欲日中，鼠入復出，出復入，轉更數語如前。

translations.literal: Just as midday was about to arrive, the rat entered and came out again, going in and out repeatedly, speaking several times as before.
translations.idiomatic: As midday approached, the rat went in and out again and again, repeating its words as before.

sentences.zh: 日適中，鼠曰：「周南，汝不應我，復何道。

translations.literal: When the sun was exactly at the center, the rat said: "Zhounan, you do not answer me—what more is there to say.
translations.idiomatic: At the exact center of the day the rat said, "Zhounan, you will not answer me—what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 」言絕，顛蹶而死，即失衣冠。

translations.literal: When the words ended, it toppled over and died; cap and robes at once vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Its speech ended; it toppled over and died, and its cap and robes vanished.

sentences.zh: 取視，俱如常鼠。

translations.literal: When taken and examined, all were like an ordinary rat.
translations.idiomatic: When they looked, it was an ordinary rat in every respect.

sentences.zh: 案班固說，此黃祥也。

translations.literal: According to Ban Gu's explanation, this was a yellow omen.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu explained that this was a yellow portent.

sentences.zh: 是時曹爽秉政，競為比周，故鼠作變也。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Shuang held power; rivals formed cliques against one another—hence the rat made this transformation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao Shuang dominated the government and factions collided against one another, so the rat took this strange form.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明七年春，太湖邊忽多鼠。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, suddenly there were many rats beside Tai Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, rats suddenly multiplied along the shore of Tai Lake.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，水至，悉變成鯉魚。

translations.literal: That summer the waters rose and all turned into carp.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the flood came, and they all turned into carp.

sentences.zh: 民人一日取，轉得三五十斛。

translations.literal: In a single day the people could catch thirty to fifty piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day the people could catch thirty to fifty piculs.

sentences.zh: 明年，大飢。

translations.literal: The following year there was great famine.
translations.idiomatic: The following year brought great famine.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興四年八月，黃霧四塞，埃氣蔽天。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, yellow fog closed in on all four sides; dust and vapor veiled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, yellow fog sealed the four quarters and dusty vapor shrouded the sky.

sentences.zh: 案楊宣對，近土氣，亂之祥也。

translations.literal: According to Yang Xuan's response, this approximates earthy qi—the omen of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan explained that this approached the qi of earth—the portent of disorder.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌二年正月癸巳，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: On the first day guisi of the first month of the second year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan of Jin, yellow fog closed in on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day guisi of the first month of the second year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan of Jin, yellow fog closed in on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和七年三月，涼州大風拔木，黃霧下塵。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Yonghe of Emperor Mu of Jin, Liangzhou had a great wind that uprooted trees; yellow fog brought down dust.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, Liangzhou had a great wind that uprooted trees, and yellow fog brought dust down from the sky.

sentences.zh: 是時張重華納譖，出謝艾為酒泉太守，而所任非其人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Chonghua heeded slander and dismissed Xie Ai from his post as governor of Jiuquan, appointing one unfit for the office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Chonghua heeded slander, dismissed Xie Ai from the governorship of Jiuquan, and appointed someone unfit for the post.

sentences.zh: 至九年死，嗣子見弒。

translations.literal: By the ninth year he was dead; the heir was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth year he was dead, and his heir was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 是其應也。

translations.literal: This was its correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: This was the correspondence.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「聞善不予，茲謂不知。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "Hearing of the good yet not bestowing reward—this is called not knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "To hear of goodness yet grant no reward is called ignorance.

sentences.zh: 厥異黃，厥咎聾，厥災不嗣。

translations.literal: Its omen is yellow; its fault is deafness; its calamity is no succession.
translations.idiomatic: Its portent is yellow; its fault is deafness; its disaster is the cutting off of succession.

sentences.zh: 黃者，有黃濁氣四塞天下，蔽賢絕道，故災至絕世也。」

translations.literal: Yellow means yellow turbid qi closing the realm on all four sides, screening the worthy and cutting off the Way—hence calamity reaches extinction of the lineage."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow means turbid yellow qi sealing the world on every side, blocking the worthy and severing the Way—so disaster ends the line."

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興元年十月丙申朔，黃霧皆濁，不雨。

translations.literal: On the first day bingshen of the tenth month of the first year of Xingyuan of Emperor An of Jin, yellow fog was all turbid and it did not rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day bingshen of the tenth month of the first year of Xingyuan under Emperor An of Jin, the yellow fog was thick and murky, and no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十八年秋七月，天有黃光，洞照于地。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, there was yellow radiance in the sky, shining through to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn of the eighteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, yellow light filled the sky and shone down upon the earth.

sentences.zh: 太子率更令何承天謂之榮光，太平之祥，上表稱慶。

translations.literal: He Chengtian, Director of the Crown Prince's Household, called it glorious radiance, an omen of great peace, and submitted a memorial of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian, Director of the Crown Prince's Household, called it glorious radiance and an omen of great peace, and submitted a memorial of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 地震

translations.literal: Earthquakes.
translations.idiomatic: Earthquakes:

sentences.zh: 吳孫權黃武四年，江東地連震。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangwu of Sun Quan of Wu, the lands east of the river shook in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangwu under Sun Quan of Wu, the lands east of the Yangzi shook again and again.

sentences.zh: 是時權受魏爵命，為大將軍、吳王，改元專制，不修臣迹。

translations.literal: At that time Quan received Wei enfeoffment and orders as Grand General and King of Wu, changed the era name and monopolized rule, and did not maintain the traces of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sun Quan accepted enfeoffment and orders from Wei as Grand General and King of Wu, changed the era name, ruled autonomously, and no longer kept the demeanor of a subject.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「臣事雖正，專必震。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "Though a minister's service is correct, if he monopolizes power there must be earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "Though a minister's conduct is upright, exclusive power will bring earthquake.

sentences.zh: 」董仲舒、劉向並云「臣下強盛，將動而為害」之應也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshen and Liu Xiang both said it is the correspondence of "powerful ministers below about to stir and do harm."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshen and Liu Xiang both said this was the correspondence of powerful ministers below stirring to do harm.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍二年十一月，京都地震，從東來，隱隱有聲，屋瓦搖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Qinglong of Emperor Ming of Wei, the capital shook; it came from the east with a faint sound, and roof tiles trembled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming of Wei, the capital shook. The tremor came from the east with a faint rumble, and roof tiles rattled.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年六月戊申，京都地震。

translations.literal: On the day wushen of the sixth month of the first year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, the capital shook.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen of the sixth month of the first year of Jingchu under Emperor Ming of Wei, the capital shook.

sentences.zh: 是秋，吳將朱然圍江夏，荊州刺史胡質擊退之。

translations.literal: That autumn the Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Jiangxia; the inspector Hu Zhi drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Jiangxia, and the inspector Hu Zhi drove him back.

sentences.zh: 又公孫淵自立為燕王，改年，置百官。

translations.literal: Also Gongsun Yuan declared himself King of Yan, changed the era name, and established the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan also declared himself King of Yan, changed the era name, and established a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 明年，討平之。

translations.literal: The following year he was suppressed and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was suppressed and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權嘉禾六年五月，江東地震。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Jiahe of Sun Quan of Wu, the lands east of the river shook.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Jiahe under Sun Quan of Wu, the lands east of the Yangzi shook.

sentences.zh: 赤烏二年正月，地又再震。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Chiwu, the ground shook again.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Chiwu, the ground shook again.

sentences.zh: 是時呂壹專政，步騭上疏曰：「伏聞校事，吹毛求瑕，趣欲陷人，成其威福，無罪無辜，橫受重刑，雖有大臣，不見信任。

translations.literal: At that time Lü Yi monopolized government. Bu Zhi submitted a memorial saying: "It is heard that the investigatorial officers blow on hairs to seek flaws, hurrying to entrap people and establish their power and favor; the guiltless and innocent suffer heavy punishments in spite; though there are great ministers, they are not seen or trusted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lü Yi dominated the government. Bu Zhi submitted a memorial saying, "I hear that investigatorial officers pick at the smallest flaws, eager to entrap men and build their power. The innocent suffer harsh punishment, and even great ministers are not trusted.

sentences.zh: 如此，天地焉得無變。

translations.literal: Thus how could Heaven and Earth be without change.
translations.idiomatic: How then could Heaven and Earth remain unchanged?

sentences.zh: 故嘉禾六年、赤烏二年，地連震動，臣下專政之應也。

translations.literal: Therefore the connected earthquakes of the sixth year of Jiahe and the second year of Chiwu are the correspondence of ministers' holding exclusive power.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the earthquakes of the sixth year of Jiahe and the second year of Chiwu were the correspondence of ministers' monopoly on power.

sentences.zh: 冀所以警悟人主，可不深思其意哉。

translations.literal: It is hoped thereby to awaken the lord of men—could he not deeply ponder its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped thereby to awaken the ruler—could the sovereign not ponder its meaning deeply?"

sentences.zh: 」壹後卒敗。

translations.literal: Yi afterward in the end was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi was eventually overthrown.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始二年十一月，南安郡地震。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Zhengshi of the Prince of Qi of Wei, Nan'an commandery shook.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Zhengshi under the Prince of Qi of Wei, Nan'an commandery shook.

sentences.zh: 正始三年七月甲申，南安郡地震；

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the seventh month of the third year of Zhengshi, Nan'an commandery shook;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen of the seventh month of the third year of Zhengshi, Nan'an commandery shook;

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏郡地震。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month, Wei commandery shook.
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month Wei commandery shook.

sentences.zh: 正始六年二月丁卯，南安郡地震。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao of the second month of the sixth year of Zhengshi, Nan'an commandery shook.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao of the second month of the sixth year of Zhengshi, Nan'an commandery shook.

sentences.zh: 是時曹爽專政，遷太后于永寧宮，太后與帝相泣而別。

translations.literal: At that time Cao Shuang monopolized government and moved the empress dowager to Yongning Palace; the empress dowager and the emperor wept as they parted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cao Shuang dominated the government, moved the empress dowager to Yongning Palace, and she and the emperor wept as they parted.

sentences.zh: 連年地震，是其應也。

translations.literal: Earthquakes year after year—this was its correspondence.
