translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's explanation: "Mountains are yang; they represent the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained: "Mountains belong to yang and stand for the ruler;

sentences.zh: 水，陰，民也。

translations.literal: water is yin; it represents the people.
translations.idiomatic: water belongs to yin and stands for the people.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，君道崩壞，百姓將失其所也」。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seems to say: The ruler's way will collapse, and the common people will lose their place."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seems to say: the ruler's way will crumble and the common people will lose their home."

sentences.zh: 與春秋梁山崩，漢齊、楚眾山發水同事也。

translations.literal: This is the same matter as when Mount Liang collapsed in the Spring and Autumn Annals and when the many mountains of Qi and Chu in Han sent forth water.
translations.idiomatic: This is the same kind of event as when Mount Liang collapsed in the Spring and Autumn Annals and when the many mountains of Qi and Chu in Han disgorged floods.

sentences.zh: 「夫三代命祀，祭不越望，吉凶禍福，不是過也」。

translations.literal: "In the three dynasties ordained sacrifices, offerings did not cross beyond what one could see from afar; fortune and misfortune did not go beyond this."
translations.idiomatic: "In the three dynasties the ordained sacrifices did not extend beyond what one could see from the border shrine; good and ill fortune did not pass beyond one's own domain."

sentences.zh: 吳雖帝，其實列國，災發丹楊，其天意矣。

translations.literal: Though Wu had an emperor, in truth it was but a feudal state; disaster arose at Danyang—this was Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wu styled itself an empire, in truth it was only a feudal state; when disaster struck Danyang, that was Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 國主山川，山崩川竭，亡之徵也。

translations.literal: The state holds lordship over mountains and rivers; when mountains collapse and rivers dry up, this is a sign of perishing.
translations.idiomatic: The state holds dominion over mountains and rivers; when mountains collapse and rivers run dry, that is a sign of extinction.

sentences.zh: 後二年而權薨，薨二十六年而吳亡。

translations.literal: Two years later Quan died; twenty-six years after his death Wu perished.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Sun Quan died; twenty-six years after his death Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙二年二月，太行山崩。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Xixi of Emperor Yuan of Wei, Mount Taihang collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Xixi under Emperor Yuan of Wei, Mount Taihang collapsed.

sentences.zh: 此魏亡之徵也。

translations.literal: This was a sign of Wei's perishing.
translations.idiomatic: This was a sign that Wei would perish.

sentences.zh: 其冬，晉有天下。

translations.literal: That winter Jin possessed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Jin took possession of the realm.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始三年三月戊子，太行山崩。

translations.literal: On the wuzi day of the third month of the third year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, Mount Taihang collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the third month of the third year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, Mount Taihang collapsed.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年七月，泰山崩，墜三里。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taishi, Mount Tai collapsed, three li falling away.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Taishi, Mount Tai collapsed and three li of its mass fell away.

sentences.zh: 此晉之咎徵也。

translations.literal: This was Jin's ominous sign.
translations.idiomatic: This was an ominous sign for Jin.

sentences.zh: 至帝晏駕，而祿去王室，懷、愍淪胥於北，元帝中興於南，是其應也。

translations.literal: When the emperor passed away, emoluments departed the royal house; Emperors Huai and Min were lost in the north, and Emperor Yuan restored the dynasty in the south—this was its correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the royal house lost its sustenance; Emperors Huai and Min were overrun in the north while Emperor Yuan revived the dynasty in the south—this was the correspondence.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「自上下者為崩，厥應泰山之石顛而下，聖王受命，人君虜。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "What falls from above to below is collapse; its correspondence is stones on Mount Tai tumbling down—a sage king receives the mandate, and the ruler becomes captive."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "What falls from on high is collapse; its correspondence is stones on Mount Tai tumbling down—the sage king receives the mandate, and the ruler is taken captive."

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康五年丙午，宣帝廟地陷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, on the bingwu day, the ground at Emperor Xuan's temple sank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, on the bingwu day the ground at Emperor Xuan's temple sank.

sentences.zh: 太康六年三月，南安新興縣山崩，涌水出。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, mountains collapsed in Nan'an and Xinxing counties, and gushing water issued forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year of Taikang, mountains collapsed in Nan'an and Xinxing counties and gushing water burst out.

sentences.zh: 太康七年七月，朱提之大瀘山崩，震壞郡舍；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Taikang, Mount Dalu in Zhuti collapsed, shaking and destroying the commandery offices;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the seventh year of Taikang, Mount Dalu in Zhuti collapsed, shaking the ground and wrecking the commandery offices;

sentences.zh: 陰平之仇池崖隕。

translations.literal: the cliffs at Chou Pool in Yinping fell.
translations.idiomatic: and the cliffs at Chou Pool in Yinping gave way.

sentences.zh: 太康八年七月，大雨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Taikang, great rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Taikang, torrential rain fell.

sentences.zh: 殿前地陷，方五尺，深數丈。

translations.literal: Before the palace hall the ground sank, five feet square and several zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: Before the palace hall the ground sank into a pit five feet square and several zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康四年五月壬子，地陷，方三十丈，殺人。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the fifth month of the fourth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, the ground sank, thirty zhang square, killing people.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the fifth month of the fourth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the ground collapsed into a pit thirty zhang across, killing people.

sentences.zh: 史闕其處。

translations.literal: The historical record omits the place.
translations.idiomatic: The historical record does not name the place.

sentences.zh: 元康四年八月，居庸地裂，廣三十丈，長百三十丈，水出殺人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Yuankang, at Juyong the ground split, thirty zhang wide and one hundred thirty zhang long; water issued forth and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Yuankang, the ground at Juyong split open thirty zhang wide and one hundred thirty zhang long; water gushed out and killed people.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉元年三月，洛陽東北步廣里地陷。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongjia of Emperor Xiao Huai of Jin, the ground sank at Buguang Ward northeast of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Xiaohuai of Jin, the ground sank at Buguang Ward northeast of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年八月乙亥，鄄城城無故自壞七十餘丈，司馬越惡之，遷于濮陽。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the eighth month of the second year of Yongjia, the wall of Yancheng city for no reason broke apart for more than seventy zhang; Sima Yue regarded it with dismay and moved to Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the eighth month of the second year of Yongjia, more than seventy zhang of the wall at Yancheng collapsed for no apparent reason; Sima Yue took it as a dire omen and moved his seat to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 此見沴之異也。

translations.literal: This was the anomaly of a malign influence made visible.
translations.idiomatic: This was a visible manifestation of malign cosmic influence.

sentences.zh: 越卒陵上，終亦受禍。

translations.literal: Yue died with disregard for his sovereign, and in the end also suffered calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yue died while lording it over his sovereign, and in the end suffered calamity himself.

sentences.zh: 永嘉三年七月戊辰，當陽地裂三所，所廣三丈，長二百餘步。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the seventh month of the third year of Yongjia, at Dangyang the ground split in three places, each three zhang wide and more than two hundred paces long.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the seventh month of the third year of Yongjia, the ground at Dangyang split open in three places, each three zhang wide and more than two hundred paces long.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「地坼裂者，臣下分離，不肯相從也。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When earth splits and cracks, ministers and subordinates separate and will not follow one another."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's "Commentary on the Changes" says: "When the earth splits and cracks, ministers and subordinates divide and refuse to follow one another."

sentences.zh: 」其後司馬越、苟晞交惡，四方牧伯莫不離散，王室遂亡。

translations.literal: Afterward Sima Yue and Gou Xi turned hostile; provincial governors throughout the four directions all scattered, and the royal house perished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Sima Yue and Gou Xi turned on each other; provincial governors throughout the realm scattered, and the royal house fell.

sentences.zh: 永嘉三年十月，宜都夷道山崩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Yongjia, Mount Yidao in Yidu collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Yongjia, Mount Yidao in Yidu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 永嘉四年四月，湘東酃黑石山崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yongjia, Mount Heishi at Ling in Xiangdong collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yongjia, Mount Heishi at Ling in Xiangdong collapsed.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興四年八月，常山崩，水出，滹沱盈溢，大木傾拔。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, Mount Chang collapsed; water issued forth, the Hutuo overflowed, and great trees were uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Mount Chang collapsed; water burst out, the Hutuo River overflowed, and great trees were uprooted.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和四年十月，柴桑廬山西北崖崩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin, the northwest cliffs of Mount Lu at Chaisang collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, the northwest cliffs of Mount Lu at Chaisang collapsed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，劉胤為郭默所殺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Liu Yin was killed by Guo Mo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Liu Yin was killed by Guo Mo.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康九年六月夜，暴雷雨。

translations.literal: On a night in the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, sudden wind and thunderstorm.
translations.idiomatic: One night in the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, a sudden thunderstorm broke.

sentences.zh: 賈謐齋屋柱陷入地，壓謐牀帳。

translations.literal: A pillar of Jia Mi's study hall sank into the ground, crushing Mi's bed curtains.
translations.idiomatic: A pillar of Jia Mi's study hall sank into the earth and crushed his bed curtains.

sentences.zh: 此木沴土，土失其性，不能載也。

translations.literal: This was wood malignly affecting earth; earth lost its nature and could not bear weight.
translations.idiomatic: This was wood malignly overcoming earth; earth lost its proper nature and could no longer bear weight.

sentences.zh: 明年，謐誅。

translations.literal: The next year Mi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jia Mi was executed.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝光熙元年五月，范陽地然，可以爨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Guangxi of Emperor Hui of Jin, the ground at Fanyang burned and could be used for cooking.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Guangxi under Emperor Hui of Jin, the ground at Fanyang caught fire and could be used to cook food.

sentences.zh: 此火沴土也。

translations.literal: This was fire malignly affecting earth.
translations.idiomatic: This was fire malignly overcoming earth.

sentences.zh: 是時禮樂征伐自諸侯出。

translations.literal: At that time ritual, music, campaigns, and punishments issued from the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: At that time ritual, music, war, and punishment all issued from the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙八年三月壬寅，山陰有聲如雷，地陷深廣各四尺。

translations.literal: On the renyin day of the third month of the eighth year of Yixi of Emperor An of Jin, at Shanyin there was a sound like thunder; the ground sank four feet deep and four feet wide.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day of the third month of the eighth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, Shanyin thundered and the ground sank into a pit four feet deep and four feet across.

sentences.zh: 義熙十年五月戊寅，西明門地穿，涌水出，毀門扇及限。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the fifth month of the tenth year of Yixi, at the Ximing Gate the ground broke through, gushing water issued forth, and destroyed the gate panels and thresholds.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the fifth month of the tenth year of Yixi, the ground at the Ximing Gate broke open, gushing water destroyed the gate panels and thresholds.

sentences.zh: 此水沴土也。

translations.literal: This was water malignly affecting earth.
translations.idiomatic: This was water malignly overcoming earth.

sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「皇之不極，是謂不建。

translations.literal: The Five Elements Treatise says: "When the imperial is without extremity, this is called failure to establish.
translations.idiomatic: The "Treatise on the Five Elements" says: "When the imperial pole is not established, this is called failure to build the foundation.

sentences.zh: 厥咎眊，厥罰恒陰，厥極弱。

translations.literal: Its blame is dim-sightedness, its punishment constant yin, its extremity weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Its fault is dim-sightedness, its punishment unending yin, its extremity weakness.

sentences.zh: 時則有射妖，時則有龍蛇之孽，時則有馬禍，時則有下人伐上之痾，時則有日月亂行，星辰逆行。」

translations.literal: Then there are shooting portents; then calamities of dragons and serpents; then equine disasters; then the malady of those below attacking those above; then sun and moon run awry and stars move retrograde."
translations.idiomatic: Then come shooting portents; then calamities of dragons and serpents; then equine disasters; then the malady of inferiors striking superiors; then sun and moon run awry and stars move backward."

sentences.zh: 常陰

translations.literal: Constant yin.
translations.idiomatic: Constant yin:

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮太平三年，自八月沈陰不雨，四十餘日。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping under Sun Liang of Wu, from the eighth month dense yin without rain lasted more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping under Sun Liang of Wu, from the eighth month a heavy, sunless gloom without rain lasted more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 是時將誅孫綝，謀泄。

translations.literal: At that time they were about to execute Sun Chen; the plot was disclosed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a plot was underway to kill Sun Chen, but the conspiracy leaked out.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，綝以兵圍宮，廢亮為會稽王。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the ninth month, Chen surrounded the palace with troops and deposed Liang as King of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the ninth month, Chen surrounded the palace with troops and deposed Liang as King of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 此常陰之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment of constant yin.
translations.idiomatic: This was the punishment of constant yin.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧寶鼎元年十二月，太史奏久陰不雨，將有陰謀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoding under Sun Hao of Wu, the Grand Astrologer reported prolonged yin without rain—there would be a yin conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoding under Sun Hao of Wu, the Grand Astrologer reported prolonged yin without rain and warned that a secret plot was forming.

sentences.zh: 晧深驚懼。

translations.literal: Hao was deeply alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was deeply alarmed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 時陸凱等謀因其謁廟廢之。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Kai and others plotted to depose him when he went to worship at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Kai and others plotted to depose him when he went out to worship at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 及出，留平領兵前驅，凱語平，平不許，是以不果。

translations.literal: When he went out, Liu Ping led troops as vanguard; Kai spoke to Ping, but Ping would not agree, and so it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao went out, Liu Ping led the vanguard; Kai confided in Ping, but Ping refused, and so the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 晧既肆虐，羣下多懷異圖，終至降亡。

translations.literal: Once Hao had tyrannized, many below harbored other designs, and in the end came surrender and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hao had turned tyrannical, many of his followers harbored other designs, and in the end the state surrendered and perished.

sentences.zh: 宋後廢帝元徽三年四月，連陰不雨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor of Song, continuous yin without rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor of Song, unbroken overcast skies brought no rain.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年八月，多陰。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Yuanhui, much yin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Yuanhui, yin predominated.

sentences.zh: 後二年，廢帝殞。

translations.literal: Two years later the Deposed Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the Deposed Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 射妖

translations.literal: Shooting portents.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting portents:

sentences.zh: 蜀車騎將軍鄧芝征涪陵，見玄猿緣山，手射中之。

translations.literal: When Deng Zhi of Shu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, campaigned against Fuling, he saw a dark ape climbing the mountain and shot it with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Zhi of Shu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, campaigned against Fuling, he saw a dark ape climbing the mountain and shot it with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 猿拔其箭，卷木葉塞其創。

translations.literal: The ape pulled out the arrow and rolled tree leaves to plug its wound.
translations.idiomatic: The ape pulled out the arrow and packed tree leaves into the wound.

sentences.zh: 芝曰：「嘻！

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾違物之性，其將死矣。

translations.literal: I have violated the nature of things; I am about to die."
translations.idiomatic: I have violated the nature of living things; I am about to die."

sentences.zh: 」俄而卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 此射妖也。

translations.literal: This was a shooting portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a shooting portent.

sentences.zh: 一曰猿母抱子，芝射中之，子為拔箭，取木葉塞創。

translations.literal: One version says: The ape mother held her young; Zhi shot and hit them; the young pulled out the arrow and took tree leaves to plug the wound.
translations.idiomatic: Another account says the mother ape was carrying her young; Zhi shot and hit them; the young pulled out the arrow and stuffed tree leaves into the wound.

sentences.zh: 芝歎息，投弓水中，自知當死矣。

translations.literal: Zhi sighed, cast his bow into the water, and knew he would die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sighed, cast his bow into the water, and knew his death was near.

sentences.zh: 晉恭帝之為琅邪王時，好奇戲，嘗閉一馬於門內，令人射之，欲觀幾箭而死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong of Jin was Prince of Langye, he delighted in curious games; once he shut a horse inside a gate and had men shoot it, wishing to see how many arrows it took to die.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong of Jin was still Prince of Langye, he delighted in strange amusements; once he shut a horse inside a gate and had men shoot it to see how many arrows it would take to kill it.

sentences.zh: 左右有諫者，曰：「馬，國姓也。

translations.literal: Attendants remonstrated, saying: "Horse is the dynastic surname.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants remonstrated with him, saying, "Horse is the dynastic surname.

sentences.zh: 而今射之，不祥甚矣。

translations.literal: To shoot it now is most inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: To shoot it now is a grave ill omen."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃止，而馬已被十許箭矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped, but the horse had already been struck by some ten arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He then stopped, but the horse had already been pierced by some ten arrows.

sentences.zh: 此蓋射妖也。

translations.literal: This was likely a shooting portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was likely a shooting portent.

sentences.zh: 俄而桓玄篡位。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 龍蛇之孽

translations.literal: Calamities of dragons and serpents.
translations.idiomatic: Portents of dragons and serpents:

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍元年正月甲申，青龍見郟之摩陂井中。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the first month of the first year of Qinglong of Emperor Ming of Wei, a green dragon appeared in a well at Mobei in Jia.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the first month of the first year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming of Wei, a green dragon appeared in a well at Mobei in Jia.

sentences.zh: 凡瑞興非時，則為妖孽，況困於井，非嘉祥矣。

translations.literal: Whenever auspicious signs arise out of season, they become demon portents; all the more when trapped in a well—this is no blessed omen.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an auspicious sign appears out of season, it becomes a portent of disaster; all the more when the creature is trapped in a well—that is no blessed omen.

sentences.zh: 魏以改年，非也。

translations.literal: Wei's changing the reign era on this account was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was wrong to change its reign title on this account.

sentences.zh: 晉武不賀，是也。

translations.literal: Jin Wu's refusing to celebrate was right.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wu was right to refuse congratulations.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「自明帝終魏世，青龍黃龍見者，皆其主廢興之應也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "From when Emperor Ming ended until the Wei era closed, appearances of green dragons and yellow dragons were all responses to the rise and fall of their rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote: "From the end of Emperor Ming's reign through the close of the Wei dynasty, every sighting of a green dragon or yellow dragon was an omen of its ruler's rise or fall."

sentences.zh: 魏土運，青，木色也，而不勝于金，黃得位，青失位之象也。

translations.literal: Wei's dynastic element was Earth; green is the color of Wood, which could not overcome Metal; yellow took the position—an image of green losing its place.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ruling element was Earth; green is Wood's color, and Wood could not prevail over Metal—yellow held the throne while green lost its seat.

sentences.zh: 青龍多見者，君德國運內相剋伐也。

translations.literal: Frequent green dragons meant the ruler's virtue and the state's fortune were mutually overcoming within.
translations.idiomatic: The many green dragons signified that royal virtue and national fortune were devouring one another from within.

sentences.zh: 故高貴鄉公卒敗于兵。

translations.literal: Therefore the Duke of Gaogui in the end was defeated by arms.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Duke of Gaogui was at last destroyed in war.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說：『龍貴象，而困井中，諸侯將有幽執之禍也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's explanation: 'The dragon is a noble image, yet trapped in a well—feudal lords will suffer the calamity of secret imprisonment.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained: "The dragon is a noble emblem, yet when it is trapped in a well, feudal lords will face the calamity of being held in secret confinement."

sentences.zh: 』魏世龍莫不在井，此居上者逼制之應。

translations.literal: ' In the Wei era dragons were never not in wells—this was the response of those above coercing and restraining.
translations.idiomatic: "Throughout Wei, dragons invariably appeared in wells—a sign that those on high were crushing and restraining their sovereign."

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公著潛龍詩，即此旨也。」

translations.literal: The Duke of Gaogui composed the 'Poem of the Hidden Dragon'—precisely this intent."
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Gaogui composed the "Poem of the Hidden Dragon"—exactly this meaning."

sentences.zh: 魏高貴鄉公正元元年冬十月戊戌，黃龍見于鄴井中。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, on the wuxu day of the winter of the first year of Zhengyuan of the Duke of Gaogui of Wei, a yellow dragon appeared in a well at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Zhengyuan under the Duke of Gaogui of Wei, on the wuxu day of the tenth month, a yellow dragon appeared in a well at Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏高貴鄉公甘露元年正月辛丑，青龍見軹縣井中；

translations.literal: In the first month, on the xinchou day of the first year of Ganlu of the Duke of Gaogui of Wei, a green dragon appeared in a well at Zhi county;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Ganlu under the Duke of Gaogui of Wei, on the xinchou day, a green dragon appeared in a well at Zhi county;

sentences.zh: 六月乙丑，青龍見元城縣界井中。

translations.literal: in the sixth month, on the yichou day, a green dragon appeared in a well on the border of Yuancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month, on the yichou day, a green dragon appeared in a well on the border of Yuancheng county.

sentences.zh: 甘露二年二月，青龍見溫縣井中。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Ganlu, a green dragon appeared in a well at Wen county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Ganlu, a green dragon appeared in a well at Wen county.

sentences.zh: 甘露三年，黃龍青龍仍見頓丘、冠軍、陽夏縣界井中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Ganlu, yellow dragons and green dragons again appeared in wells on the borders of Dunqiu, Guanjun, and Yangxia counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Ganlu, yellow and green dragons again appeared in wells on the borders of Dunqiu, Guanjun, and Yangxia counties.

sentences.zh: 景元三年二月，青龍見軹縣井中。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Jingyuan, a green dragon appeared in a well at Zhi county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Jingyuan, a green dragon appeared in a well at Zhi county.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧天冊中，龍乳於長沙民家，啖鷄鶵。

translations.literal: During the Tian Ce era of Sun Hao of Wu, a dragon nursed in a commoner's house at Changsha and ate chicks.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiance reign of Sun Hao of Wu, a dragon nursed in a commoner's house in Changsha and devoured chicks.

sentences.zh: 京房易妖曰：「龍乳人家，王者為庶人。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi omens say: "When a dragon nurses in a man's house, the king becomes a commoner."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes omens say: "When a dragon nurses in a commoner's home, the king will become a commoner."

sentences.zh: 」其後晧降。

translations.literal: Afterward Hao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hao surrendered.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧二年六月丙申，白龍二見于九原井中。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day of the sixth month of the second year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, two white dragons appeared in a well at Jiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the sixth month of the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, two white dragons appeared in a well at Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康五年正月癸卯，二龍見于武庫井中。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the first month of the fifth year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin, two dragons appeared in the arsenal well.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the first month of the fifth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, two dragons appeared in the arsenal well.

sentences.zh: 帝見龍，有喜色，百僚將賀。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the dragons and showed pleasure; the hundred officials were about to congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw the dragons, his face brightened; the court officials prepared to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 劉毅獨表曰：「昔龍漦夏庭，禍發周室；

translations.literal: Liu Yi alone submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly dragon spittle appeared in the Xia court, and disaster arose in the Zhou house;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi alone submitted a memorial: "Long ago dragon spittle appeared in the Xia court, and calamity broke out in the house of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 龍見鄭門，子產不賀。

translations.literal: a dragon appeared at the gate of Zheng, and Zichan did not congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: when a dragon appeared at the gate of Zheng, Zichan refused to congratulate."

sentences.zh: 」帝答曰：「朕德政未修，未有以膺受嘉祥。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "My virtuous government is not yet perfected; I have no grounds to receive such auspicious signs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "My virtuous rule is not yet perfected; I have no grounds on which to accept such auspicious signs."

sentences.zh: 」遂不賀也。

translations.literal: Thereupon congratulations were not offered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon no congratulations were offered.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：「龍，水物也，何與於人，子產言之當矣。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: "The dragon is a creature of water—what has it to do with men? Zichan's words were apt.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng wrote: "The dragon belongs to the element of water—what has it to do with mankind? Zichan spoke rightly.

sentences.zh: 但非其所處，實為妖災。

translations.literal: Yet when it is not in its proper place, it is truly a demon calamity.
translations.idiomatic: But when it appears out of its proper place, it is truly a demonic calamity.

sentences.zh: 夫龍以飛翔顯見為美，則潛伏幽處，非休祥也。

translations.literal: The dragon's beauty lies in soaring and manifest flight; to lurk in a hidden place is no blessed omen.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon's glory lies in soaring aloft for all to see; to lurk in some hidden recess is no blessed omen.

sentences.zh: 漢惠帝二年，兩龍見蘭陵井中，本志以為其後趙王幽死之象也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Hui of Han, two dragons appeared in a well at Lanling; this Treatise takes it as the image of the Prince of Zhao's later death by imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Hui of Han, two dragons appeared in a well at Lanling; this Treatise regards it as the omen of the Prince of Zhao's later death in confinement.

sentences.zh: 武庫者，帝王威御之器所寶藏也，室宇邃密，非龍所處。

translations.literal: The arsenal is where the emperor's awe-inspiring weapons are stored; the chambers are deep and sealed—not a place for dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The arsenal is where the emperor's awe-inspiring weapons are stored; its chambers are deep and sealed—not a place for dragons.

sentences.zh: 後七年，蕃王相害，二十八年，果有二胡僭竊神器。

translations.literal: Seven years later feudal princes harmed one another; twenty-eight years later, two barbarians indeed usurped the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later the feudal princes turned on one another; twenty-eight years later, two barbarian chieftains indeed usurped the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 勒、虎二逆皆字曰龍，此之表異，為有證矣。

translations.literal: The two rebels Le and Hu both bore the style-name Long—this portent had clear proof."
translations.idiomatic: The two rebels Shi Le and Shi Hu both used Long as their style name—here the omen found its proof."

sentences.zh: 」史臣案龍為休瑞，而屈於井中，前史言之已詳。

translations.literal: The historiographer notes: The dragon is a blessed omen, yet humbled in a well—earlier histories have spoken of this at length.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: The dragon is a blessed omen, yet when it is humbled in a well, earlier histories have already spoken at length.

sentences.zh: 但兆幽微，非可臆斷，故五行、符瑞兩存之。

translations.literal: But the portent is subtle and cannot be guessed at will; therefore both the Five Elements and auspicious omens sections preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the omen is subtle and cannot be guessed at will; therefore both the Five Elements and the auspicious-omens sections preserve the record.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興二年十一月，枹罕羌妓產一龍子，色似錦文，嘗就母乳，遙見神光，少得就視。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, a Qiang courtesan of Fuhan gave birth to a dragon child, its color like brocade patterns; when it nursed at the breast, a divine light was seen from afar, and few could approach to look.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, a Qiang courtesan of Fuhan gave birth to a dragon child patterned like brocade; when it nursed, a divine light shone from afar, and few dared approach for a closer look.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧中，司徒府有二大蛇，長十許丈，居聽事平橑上，數年而人不知，但怪府中數失小兒及猪犬之屬。

translations.literal: During Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, in the Minister of Education's office were two great serpents, more than ten zhang long, dwelling on the rafters of the audience hall; for years no one knew, but they wondered that the office repeatedly lost small children and pigs and dogs and the like.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianning era under Emperor Wu of Jin, two great serpents more than ten zhang long lived on the rafters of the audience hall in the Minister of Education's office; for years no one knew, though people wondered why the office kept losing small children, pigs, and dogs.

sentences.zh: 後一蛇夜出，傷於刃，不能去，乃覺之。

translations.literal: Later one serpent came out at night, was wounded by a blade, and could not leave—then they became aware.
translations.idiomatic: Later one serpent emerged at night, was wounded by a blade, and could not retreat—only then was it discovered.

sentences.zh: 發徒攻擊，移時乃死。

translations.literal: Laborers were sent to attack it; after a time it died.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers were sent to kill it; after some time it died.

sentences.zh: 夫司徒五教之府，此皇極不建，故蛇孽見之。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education is the office of the five teachings—here the supreme pole was not established, hence the serpent portent appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education is the seat of the five teachings—here the supreme pole was not firmly established, and so the serpent omen appeared.

sentences.zh: 漢靈帝時，蛇見御座，楊賜以為帝溺於色之應也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ling of Han, a serpent appeared on the imperial seat; Yang Ci took it as the response to the emperor drowning in lust.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Ling of Han, a serpent appeared on the imperial throne; Yang Ci interpreted it as a sign that the emperor was drowning in lust.

sentences.zh: 魏氏宮人猥多，晉又過之，宴游是湎，此其孽也。

translations.literal: Wei had excessive palace women; Jin surpassed it still further, drowning in feasts and tours—this was its portent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei already had an excessive number of palace women; Jin surpassed it, drowning in feasts and pleasure outings—this was the omen.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「惟虺惟蛇，女子之祥。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Only the viper, only the serpent—a woman's omen."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Only the viper, only the serpent—the omen of a woman."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康五年三月癸巳，臨菑有大蛇長十餘丈，負二小蛇，入城北門，徑從市入漢城陽景王祠中不見。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the third month of the fifth year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, at Linzi was a great serpent more than ten zhang long, carrying two small serpents; it entered the north gate of the city, went straight through the market into the shrine of King Jing of Chengyang of Han, and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the third month of the fifth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, at Linzi a great serpent more than ten zhang long, bearing two small serpents on its back, entered the city's north gate, passed straight through the market into the shrine of King Jing of Chengyang of Han, and disappeared.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，齊方有劉章定傾之功，若不厲節忠慎，又將蹈章失職奪功之辱也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Qi will have Liu Zhang's merit in stabilizing the state; if one does not uphold integrity and loyal caution, one will again tread Zhang's shame of losing office and having merit seized.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Qi would soon have a Liu Zhang who steadied the realm—but if he did not hold fast to integrity and loyal caution, he would repeat Zhang's disgrace of losing office and having his merit stripped away.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏不悟，雖建興復之功，而以驕陵取禍。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong did not understand; though he had the merit of restoring the Jianxing reign, through arrogance and bullying he brought calamity on himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, did not understand; though he had restored the dynasty at Jianxing, through arrogance and bullying he brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 負二小蛇出朝市，皆有象類也。

translations.literal: Carrying two small serpents and going out into the market and court—all had their symbolic types.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing two small serpents and emerging into the market and the court—all had their symbolic counterparts.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧初，武昌有大蛇，常居故神祠空樹中，每出頭從人受食。

translations.literal: In the early Taining era of Emperor Ming of Jin, at Wuchang was a great serpent that constantly dwelt in the hollow tree of an old shrine; each time it thrust out its head to receive food from people.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Taining era under Emperor Ming of Jin, at Wuchang a great serpent constantly dwelt in the hollow of an old shrine tree and thrust out its head to be fed by passersby.

sentences.zh: 京房易妖曰：「蛇見於邑，不出三年，有大兵。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi omens say: "When a serpent appears in a town, within three years there will be great armies.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes omens say: "When a serpent appears in a settlement, within three years great armies will come.

sentences.zh: 國有大憂。

translations.literal: The state will have great sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: The state will know great sorrow."

sentences.zh: 」其後討滅王敦及其黨與。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Dun and his faction were destroyed in punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang Dun and his faction were destroyed in punitive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 馬禍

translations.literal: Horse portents.
translations.idiomatic: Horse portents:

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太熙原年，遼東有馬生角，在兩耳下，長三寸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixi of Emperor Wu of Jin, in Liaodong a horse grew horns beneath both ears, three inches long.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taixi under Emperor Wu of Jin, in Liaodong a horse grew horns beneath both ears, three inches long.

sentences.zh: 按劉向說，此兵象也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's explanation, this is the image of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xiang's explanation, this is an omen of war.

sentences.zh: 及帝晏駕之後，王室毒於兵禍，是其應也。

translations.literal: After the emperor's death, the royal house was poisoned by the calamity of arms—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, the royal house was ravaged by war—this was the fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「臣易上，政不順，厥妖馬生角。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi Tradition says: "When ministers displace their superiors and government is not compliant, the demon is a horse growing horns."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes says: "When ministers displace their superiors and government is not compliant, the portent is a horse growing horns."

sentences.zh: 」又有「天子親伐，馬生角」。

translations.literal: There is also "when the Son of Heaven campaigns in person, horses grow horns."
translations.idiomatic: There is also: "When the Son of Heaven campaigns in person, horses grow horns."

sentences.zh: 呂氏春秋曰：「人君失道，馬有生角。」

translations.literal: Master Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals says: "When the ruler loses the Way, horses grow horns."
translations.idiomatic: Master Lü's Spring and Autumn Annals says: "When a ruler loses the Way, horses grow horns."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康元年十二月，皇太子將釋奠，太傅趙王倫驂乘，至南城門，馬止，力士推之不能動。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, when the crown prince was to perform the capping sacrifice, Grand Tutor Prince of Zhao Lun rode as outrider; reaching the south gate of the city, the horse stopped and strong men could not push it forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, when the crown prince was to perform the capping sacrifice, Grand Tutor Prince of Zhao Lun rode as outrider; at the south gate the horse halted, and even strong men could not push it forward.

sentences.zh: 倫入軺車，乃進。

translations.literal: Lun entered a light carriage, and only then did it advance.
translations.idiomatic: Lun entered a light carriage, and only then did it move on.

sentences.zh: 此馬禍也。

translations.literal: This was a horse portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a horse portent.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，倫不知義方，終為亂逆，非傅導行禮之人。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Lun did not know righteousness and propriety; in the end he would become a rebel and traitor—not a man to tutor and conduct ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Lun did not know righteousness and propriety; in the end he would become a rebel and traitor—not a man fit to tutor the heir and conduct ritual.

sentences.zh: 倫不悟，故亡。

translations.literal: Lun did not understand, and therefore perished.
translations.idiomatic: Lun did not understand, and therefore perished.

sentences.zh: 元康九年十一月戊寅冬，有牝騮馬驚奔至廷尉訊堂，悲鳴而死。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the eleventh month of the ninth year of Yuankang, in winter, a mare in heat ran in panic to the interrogation hall of the Minister of Justice, wailed in grief, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of the eleventh month in the winter of the ninth year of Yuankang, a mare in heat ran in panic to the interrogation hall of the Minister of Justice, wailed in grief, and died.

sentences.zh: 是殆愍懷冤死之象也。

translations.literal: This was likely the image of Prince Huai's wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: This was likely the omen of Prince Huai's wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 見廷尉訊堂，又天意乎。

translations.literal: That it appeared at the Minister of Justice interrogation hall—was this also Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: That it appeared at the Minister of Justice's interrogation hall—was that also Heaven's intent?

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉六年二月，神馬鳴南城門。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, a divine horse neighed at the south gate of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin, a divine horse neighed at the south gate of the capital.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興二年，丹陽郡吏濮陽楊演馬生駒，兩頭自頸前別，生而死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin, Yang Yan, a clerk of Danyang commandery living at Jiyang, had a mare foal with two heads separate from the neck forward; it was born and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Yang Yan, a clerk of Danyang commandery living at Jiyang, had a mare foal with two heads branching from the neck forward; it was born and died at once.

sentences.zh: 按司馬彪說，政在私門，二頭之象也。

translations.literal: According to Sima Biao's explanation, government lay in private hands—an image of two heads.
translations.idiomatic: According to Sima Biao's explanation, government lay in private hands—an omen of two heads.

sentences.zh: 是後王敦陵上。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Dun bullied his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang Dun bullied his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康八年五月甲戌，有馬色赤如血，自宣陽門直走入于殿前，盤旋走出，尋逐莫知所在。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Xiankang of Emperor Cheng of Jin, a horse the color of blood-red ran straight in from Xuanyang Gate into the hall forecourt, circled and ran out; pursued, no one knew where it went.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the fifth month of the eighth year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, a horse the color of blood ran straight in from Xuanyang Gate into the hall forecourt, circled, and fled; though pursued, none could tell where it went.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝不豫，六月崩。

translations.literal: On the jimao day the emperor fell ill; in the sixth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day the emperor fell ill; in the sixth month he died.

sentences.zh: 此馬禍，又赤祥也。

translations.literal: This was a horse portent, and also a red omen.
translations.idiomatic: This was a horse portent, and also a red omen.

sentences.zh: 張重華在涼州，將誅其西河相張祚，祚廄馬數十匹，同時悉皆無後尾。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chonghua was in Liang province, about to execute his Xihai chancellor Zhang Zuo, several dozen horses in Zuo's stable at once all lost their tails entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chonghua was in Liang province, about to execute his Xihai chancellor Zhang Zuo, several dozen horses in Zuo's stable at once lost their tails entirely.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安四年十月，梁州有馬生角，刺史郭銓送示都督桓玄。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Long'an of Emperor An of Jin, in Liang province a horse grew horns; Governor Guo Quan sent it to show Supervisor-General Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Long'an under Emperor An of Jin, in Liang province a horse grew horns; Governor Guo Quan sent it to display to Supervisor-General Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，馬不當生角，由玄不當舉兵向上也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's explanation, horses ought not grow horns—because Xuan ought not to raise arms against his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: According to Liu Xiang's explanation, horses ought not grow horns—because Xuan ought not to have raised arms against his superiors.

sentences.zh: 覩災不悟，故至夷滅。

translations.literal: Seeing the calamity and not understanding, he therefore reached extermination.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the calamity and did not understand, and therefore was utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 人痾

translations.literal: Human anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Human anomalies:

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初初，清河宋士宗母化為鼈，入水。

translations.literal: In the early Huangchu era of Emperor Wen of Wei, the mother of Song Shizong of Qinghe transformed into a turtle and entered the water.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Huangchu era under Emperor Wen of Wei, the mother of Song Shizong of Qinghe transformed into a turtle and entered the water.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和三年，曹休部曲兵奚農女死復生。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe of Emperor Ming of Wei, Xi Nong, a woman of the troops under Cao Xiu, died and came back to life.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe under Emperor Ming of Wei, Xi Nong, a woman among the troops under Cao Xiu, died and came back to life.

sentences.zh: 時人有開周世冢，得殉葬女子，數日而有氣，數月而能語。

translations.literal: At the time someone opened a Zhou-era tomb and obtained a sacrificial woman; after several days she had breath, and after several months she could speak.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone opened a Zhou-era tomb and found a sacrificial woman; after several days she drew breath, and after several months she could speak.

sentences.zh: 郭太后愛養之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Guo took her in and raised her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Guo took her in and raised her.

sentences.zh: 又太原民發冢破棺，棺中有一生婦人，問其本事，不知也。

translations.literal: Also, a man of Taiyuan opened a tomb and broke the coffin; inside the coffin was a living woman; asked about her origins, she did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Also, a man of Taiyuan opened a tomb and broke open the coffin; inside was a living woman; asked about her origins, she did not know.

sentences.zh: 視其墓木，可三十歲。

translations.literal: Judging from the tomb timber, it could have been thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from the tomb timber, it could have been thirty years.

sentences.zh: 案京房易傳，至陰為陽，下人為上，晉宣王起之象也。

translations.literal: According to Jing Fang's Yi Tradition, when extreme yin becomes yang and inferiors become superiors, this is the image of the rise of the Jin dynastic founder.
translations.idiomatic: According to Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes, when extreme yin becomes yang and inferiors become superiors, this is the omen of the rise of the Jin dynastic founder.

sentences.zh: 漢平帝、獻帝並有此異，占以為王莽、曹操之徵。

translations.literal: Emperors Ping and Xian of Han both had this anomaly; divination took it as the sign of Wang Mang and Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Ping and Xian of Han both had this anomaly; diviners took it as the sign of Wang Mang and Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 公孫淵炊，有小兒蒸死甑中，其後夷滅。

translations.literal: When Gongsun Yuan cooked, a small child was steamed to death in the pot; afterward he was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Yuan was cooking, a small child was steamed to death in the pot; afterward he was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興二年，諸葛恪將征淮南，有孝子著衰衣入其閤。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianxing of Sun Liang of Wu, when Zhuge Ke was about to campaign against Huainan, a filial son wearing mourning garments entered his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, when Zhuge Ke was about to campaign against Huainan, a filial son in mourning garments entered his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 詰問，答曰：「不自覺入也。

translations.literal: Interrogated, he answered: "I entered without being aware."
translations.idiomatic: When questioned, he answered, "I entered without knowing how."

sentences.zh: 」時中外守備，亦悉不見。

translations.literal: At the time inner and outer guards were all in place, yet none saw him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time inner and outer guards were all in place, yet none had seen him enter.

sentences.zh: 眾皆異之。

translations.literal: The crowd all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone regarded it as strange.

sentences.zh: 及還，果見殺。

translations.literal: When he returned, he was indeed killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he was indeed killed.

sentences.zh: 恪已被害，妻在室，使婢沃盥，聞婢血臰。

translations.literal: After Ke had been killed, his wife was in the chamber and had a maid pour water for washing; she smelled blood and stench on the maid.
translations.idiomatic: After Ke had been killed, his wife was in the chamber and had a maid pour water for washing; she smelled blood and stench on the maid.

sentences.zh: 又眼目視瞻非常，妻問其故，婢蹷然躍起，頭至棟，攘臂切齒曰：「諸葛公乃為峻所殺。」

translations.literal: Also the maid's eyes and gaze were unusual; the wife asked the reason, and the maid suddenly leaped up, her head reaching the rafters, flung her arms and gnashed her teeth, saying: "Lord Zhuge was killed by Sun Jun."
translations.idiomatic: The maid's eyes and gaze were also strange; when the wife asked why, the maid suddenly leaped up, her head reaching the rafters, flung her arms and gnashed her teeth, crying: "Lord Zhuge was killed by Sun Jun!"

sentences.zh: 吳孫休永安四年，安吳民陳焦死七日，復穿冢出。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yong'an of Sun Xiu of Wu, Chen Jiao of Anwu died for seven days, then broke through the tomb and came out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, Chen Jiao of Anwu had been dead seven days when he broke through the tomb and came out.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「此與漢宣帝同事。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "This is the same matter as Emperor Xuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote: "This is the same matter as under Emperor Xuan of Han.

sentences.zh: 烏程侯晧承廢故之家，得位之祥也。」

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wucheng Hao inherited a deposed house and gained the throne—an auspicious sign of obtaining the position."
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wucheng, Hao, inherited a deposed house and gained the throne—an auspicious sign of taking the position."

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧寶鼎元年，丹陽宣騫母，年八十，因浴化為黿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding of Sun Hao of Wu, the mother of Xuan Qian of Danyang, aged eighty, because of bathing transformed into a soft-shelled turtle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding under Sun Hao of Wu, the mother of Xuan Qian of Danyang, aged eighty, transformed into a soft-shelled turtle while bathing.

sentences.zh: 兄弟閉戶衞之，掘堂上作大坎，實水其中。

translations.literal: Her brothers shut the door to guard her and dug a great pit in the hall, filling it with water.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers shut the door to guard her and dug a great pit in the hall, filling it with water.

sentences.zh: 黿入坎戲一二日，恒延頸外望，伺戶小開，便輪轉自躍，入于遠潭，遂不復還。

translations.literal: The turtle entered the pit and sported for a day or two, constantly stretching its neck to look outside; when the door opened a little, it would wheel and leap by itself into a distant pool and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: The turtle entered the pit and sported for a day or two, constantly stretching its neck to look outside; when the door opened even a little, it would wheel and leap into a distant pool and never returned.

sentences.zh: 與漢靈帝時黃氏母事同。

translations.literal: It was the same as the affair of the mother surnamed Huang in the time of Emperor Ling of Han.
translations.idiomatic: It was the same as the affair of the mother surnamed Huang in the time of Emperor Ling of Han.

sentences.zh: 吳亡之象也。

translations.literal: An image of Wu's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: An omen of Wu's destruction.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙二年八月，襄武縣言有大人見，長三丈餘，跡長三尺二寸，髮白，著黃巾黃單衣，柱杖，呼民王始語曰：「今當太平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Xianxi of Emperor Yuan of Wei, Xiangwu county reported that a great man was seen, more than three zhang tall, with footprints three chi two inches long, white-haired, wearing a yellow headcloth and yellow single garment, leaning on a staff, calling to the commoner Wang Shi and saying: "Peace is about to come."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Xianxi under Emperor Yuan of Wei, Xiangwu county reported that a giant was seen, more than three zhang tall, with footprints three chi two inches long, white-haired, wearing a yellow headcloth and yellow single robe, leaning on a staff, who called to the commoner Wang Shi and said: "Peace is about to come."

sentences.zh: 」尋晉代魏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jin replaced Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin replaced Wei.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始五年，元城人年七十，生角。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, a man of Yuancheng aged seventy grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, a man of Yuancheng aged seventy grew horns.

sentences.zh: 案漢志說，殆趙王倫篡亂之象也。

translations.literal: According to the Han Treatise's explanation, this was likely the image of Prince of Zhao Lun's usurpation and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Han Treatise's explanation, this was likely the omen of Prince of Zhao Lun's usurpation and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧二年二月，琅邪人顏畿病死，棺斂已久，家人咸夢畿謂己曰：「我當復生，可急開棺。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Xianning of Emperor Wu of Jin, Yan Ji of Langye died of illness; the coffin had been closed for a long time, and the whole family all dreamed that Ji told them: "I am about to return to life—quickly open the coffin."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, Yan Ji of Langye died of illness; the coffin had been sealed for a long time when the whole family dreamed that Ji told them: "I am about to return to life—open the coffin at once."

sentences.zh: 」遂出之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was taken out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was taken out.

sentences.zh: 漸能飲食屈申視瞻，不能行語也。

translations.literal: Gradually he could drink and eat, bend and stretch, and see and look about, but could not walk or speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he could drink and eat, bend and stretch, and look about, but could not walk or speak.

sentences.zh: 二年復死。

translations.literal: Two years later he died again.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died again.

sentences.zh: 其後劉淵、石勒遂亡晉室。

translations.literal: Afterward Liu Yuan and Shi Le then destroyed the house of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Liu Yuan and Shi Le destroyed the house of Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中，安豐有女子周世寧，年八歲，漸化為男，至十七八，而氣性成。

translations.literal: During Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, at Anfeng was a woman Zhou Shining, eight years old, who gradually transformed into a man; by seventeen or eighteen her masculine nature was fully formed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuankang era under Emperor Hui of Jin, at Anfeng a woman named Zhou Shining, eight years old, gradually transformed into a man; by seventeen or eighteen her masculine nature was fully formed.

sentences.zh: 此劉淵、石勒蕩覆晉室之妖也。

translations.literal: This was the demon of Liu Yuan and Shi Le overturning and destroying the house of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: This was the portent of Liu Yuan and Shi Le overturning and destroying the house of Jin.

sentences.zh: 漢哀帝、獻帝時並有此異，皆有易代之兆。

translations.literal: Emperors Ai and Xian of Han both had this anomaly; all had omens of changing dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Ai and Xian of Han both had this anomaly; each foretold a change of dynasty.

sentences.zh: 京房傳曰：「女子化為丈夫，茲謂陰昌，賤人為王。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Tradition says: "When a woman transforms into a man, this is called yin flourishing; base men become kings.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition says: "When a woman transforms into a man, this is called yin flourishing—base men become kings.

sentences.zh: 丈夫化為女子，茲謂陰勝陽，厥咎亡。」

translations.literal: When a man transforms into a woman, this is called yin overcoming yang; the fault is extinction."
translations.idiomatic: When a man transforms into a woman, this is called yin overcoming yang; the penalty is extinction."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧初，齊王冏唱義兵，誅除亂逆，乘輿反正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning of Emperor Hui of Jin, Prince of Qi Sima Jiong raised righteous troops and executed rebels and traitors; the imperial carriage returned to correctness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongning under Emperor Hui of Jin, the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, raised righteous troops and executed rebels and traitors; the imperial carriage returned to its proper course.

sentences.zh: 忽有婦人詣大司馬門求寄產。

translations.literal: Suddenly a woman came to the Grand Marshal's gate seeking lodging to give birth.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a woman came to the Grand Marshal's gate seeking lodging to give birth.

sentences.zh: 門者詰之，婦人曰：「我截齊便去耳。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper questioned her; the woman said: "I will cut Qi and then go."
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper questioned her; the woman said, "I will cut down Qi and then go."

sentences.zh: 」是時齊王冏匡復王室，天下歸功。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Qi Jiong restored the royal house; the world attributed merit to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Qi, Jiong, had restored the royal house; the world attributed merit to him.

sentences.zh: 識者為其惡之。

translations.literal: Those who understood regarded it as inauspicious for him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood the omen regarded it as inauspicious for him.

sentences.zh: 後果斬戮。

translations.literal: Afterward he was indeed executed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was indeed executed.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年十二月甲子，有白頭公入齊王冏大司馬府，大呼有大兵起，不出甲子旬。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the twelfth month of the first year of Yongning, a white-haired old man entered the Grand Marshal's residence of Prince of Qi Jiong, shouting that great armies would rise, and that it would not pass the ten-day jiazi cycle.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the twelfth month of the first year of Yongning, a white-haired old man entered the Grand Marshal's residence of the Prince of Qi, Jiong, shouting that great armies would rise and that it would happen within the ten-day jiazi cycle.

sentences.zh: 冏殺之。

translations.literal: Jiong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong killed him.

sentences.zh: 明年十二月戊辰，冏敗，即甲子旬也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the following year, on the wuchen day, Jiong was defeated—precisely within the jiazi ten-day cycle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the following year, on the wuchen day, Jiong was defeated—precisely within the jiazi ten-day cycle.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安元年四月癸酉，有人自雲龍門入殿前，北面再拜曰：「我當作中書監。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the fourth month of the first year of Taian of Emperor Hui of Jin, a man entered from the Yunlong Gate into the forecourt of the hall, faced north, bowed twice, and said: "I am to become Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the fourth month of the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui of Jin, a man entered through the Yunlong Gate into the hall forecourt, faced north, bowed twice, and said: "I am to become Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 」即收斬之。

translations.literal: He was immediately seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「夫禁庭，尊祕之處，今賤人徑入，而門衞不覺者，宮室將虛，而下人踰之之妖也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The forbidden court is a place of august secrecy; now a base man entered straight in while gate guards were unaware—the palace quarters will become empty and inferiors will overstep—this is its demon.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote: "The forbidden court is a place of august secrecy; when a base man enters unawares while the gate guards notice nothing, the palace will stand empty and inferiors will overstep their bounds—this is its portent.

sentences.zh: 」是後帝北遷鄴，又西遷長安，盜賊蹈藉宮闕，遂亡天下。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor moved north to Ye, then west to Chang'an; bandits trampled the palaces, and the realm was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor moved north to Ye, then west to Chang'an; bandits trampled the palaces, and the realm was lost.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝世，梁國女子許嫁，已受禮娉，尋而其夫戍長安，經年不歸。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in Liang commandery a woman had been betrothed and had received betrothal gifts; soon her husband garrisoned Chang'an and did not return for years.
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in Liang commandery a woman had been betrothed and had received betrothal gifts; soon her husband was garrisoned at Chang'an and did not return for years.

sentences.zh: 女家更以適人，女不樂行，其父母逼強，不得已而去，尋得病亡。

translations.literal: The woman's family gave her again in marriage; the woman was unwilling to go; her parents forced her, and she had no choice but to leave; soon she fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: The woman's family gave her in marriage again; she was unwilling to go, but her parents forced her, and she had no choice but to leave; soon she fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 後其夫還，問女所在，其家具說之。

translations.literal: Later her husband returned and asked where the woman was; her family told him the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later her husband returned and asked where the woman was; her family told him the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 其夫徑至女墓，不勝哀情，便發冢開棺，女遂活，因與俱歸。

translations.literal: Her husband went straight to the woman's tomb, unable to bear his grief, opened the tomb and coffin, and the woman then lived; they returned home together.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband went straight to the woman's tomb, unable to bear his grief, opened the tomb and coffin, and the woman came back to life; they returned home together.

sentences.zh: 後婿聞之，詣官爭之，所在不能決。

translations.literal: Later the second husband heard of it, went to the authorities to dispute it, and wherever he went no decision could be made.
translations.idiomatic: Later the second husband heard of it and went to the authorities to dispute the matter; wherever the case was heard, no decision could be made.

sentences.zh: 祕書郎王導議曰：「此是非常事，不得以常理斷之，宜還前夫。

translations.literal: Secretary Lang Wang Dao deliberated: "This is an extraordinary matter and cannot be judged by ordinary principle; she should be returned to the former husband."
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Lang Wang Dao ruled: "This is an extraordinary matter and cannot be judged by ordinary principle; she should be returned to her former husband."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從其議。

translations.literal: The court followed his deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed his ruling.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝世，杜錫家葬，而婢誤不得出。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Hui of Jin, at Du Xi's house there was a burial, and a maid by mistake was not taken out.
translations.idiomatic: In the era of Emperor Hui of Jin, at Du Xi's house there was a burial, and a maid by mistake was not taken out of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，開冢祔葬，而婢尚生。

translations.literal: More than ten years later the tomb was opened for a joint burial, and the maid was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later the tomb was opened for a joint burial, and the maid was still alive.

sentences.zh: 其始如瞑，有頃漸覺。

translations.literal: At first she was as if in sleep; after a while she gradually awakened.
translations.idiomatic: At first she was as if asleep; after a while she gradually awakened.

sentences.zh: 問之，自謂當一再宿耳。

translations.literal: Asked about it, she herself said she thought it had been only one or two nights.
translations.idiomatic: When asked, she herself said she thought it had been only one or two nights.

sentences.zh: 初婢之埋，年十五六，及開冢更生，猶十五六也。

translations.literal: When the maid was buried she was fifteen or sixteen; when the tomb was opened and she lived again, she was still fifteen or sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: When the maid was buried she was fifteen or sixteen; when the tomb was opened and she lived again, she was still fifteen or sixteen.

sentences.zh: 嫁之有子。

translations.literal: Given in marriage, she bore children.
translations.idiomatic: Given in marriage, she bore children.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝光熙元年，會稽謝真生子，大頭有鬢，兩蹠反向上，有男女兩體。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxi of Emperor Hui of Jin, Xie Zhen of Kuaiji had a son born with a large head and sideburns, both soles turned upward, with both male and female bodies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxi under Emperor Hui of Jin, Xie Zhen of Kuaiji had a son born with a large head and sideburns, both soles turned upward, with both male and female bodies.

sentences.zh: 生便作丈夫聲，經日死。

translations.literal: At birth he made a man's voice; after a day he died.
translations.idiomatic: At birth he spoke in a man's voice; after a day he died.

sentences.zh: 晉惠、懷之世，京、洛有兼男女體，亦能兩用人道，而性尤淫。

translations.literal: In the eras of Emperor Hui and Huai of Jin, in the capital and Luoyang there were persons with both male and female bodies who could also use both ways of intercourse, and their nature was especially licentious.
translations.idiomatic: In the eras of Emperors Hui and Huai of Jin, in the capital and Luoyang there were persons with both male and female bodies who could use both ways of intercourse, and their nature was especially licentious.

sentences.zh: 案此亂氣之所生也。

translations.literal: According to this, it was what chaotic qi produced.
translations.idiomatic: According to this record, it was what chaotic qi produced.

sentences.zh: 自咸寧、太康之後，男寵大興，甚於女色，士大夫莫不尚之，天下皆相放効，或有至夫婦離絕，怨曠妬忌者。

translations.literal: From Xianning and Taikang onward, male favorites rose greatly, surpassing love of women; scholar-officials all esteemed it, and the world mutually imitated it, some even to the point of husbands and wives separating and resentment, loneliness, and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xianning and Taikang eras onward, male favorites flourished beyond love of women; scholar-officials all esteemed it, and the world imitated one another, some even to the point of husbands and wives parting in resentment, loneliness, and jealousy.

sentences.zh: 故男女氣亂，而妖形作也。

translations.literal: Therefore male and female qi were disordered, and demon forms appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore male and female qi fell into disorder, and demonic forms appeared.

sentences.zh: 元帝太興初，又有女子陰在腹上，在揚州，性亦淫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing of Emperor Yuan, there was again a woman whose yin was on her belly, in Yang province, and her nature was also licentious.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, there was again a woman whose yin was on her belly, in Yang province, and her nature was also licentious.

sentences.zh: 京房易妖曰：「人生子，陰在首，天下大亂；

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yi omens say: "When a person bears a child and the yin is on the head, the realm will know great disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes omens say: "When a person bears a child and the yin is on the head, the realm will know great disorder;

sentences.zh: 在腹，天下有事；

translations.literal: on the belly, the realm will have affairs;
translations.idiomatic: on the belly, the realm will have affairs;

sentences.zh: 在背，天下無後。」

translations.literal: on the back, the realm will have no heirs."
translations.idiomatic: on the back, the realm will have no heirs."

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉元年，吳郡吳縣萬祥婢生子，鳥頭，兩足馬蹄，一手無毛，黃色，大如枕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, the maid of Wan Xiang of Wu county in Wu commandery bore a child with a bird's head, two feet like horse hooves, one hand without hair, yellow in color, large as a pillow.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin, the maid of Wan Xiang of Wu county in Wu commandery bore a child with a bird's head, two feet like horse hooves, one hand hairless and yellow, large as a pillow.

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興四年，新蔡縣吏任僑妻胡，年二十五，產二女，相向，腹心合同，自胸以上，齊以下，各分。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianxing of Emperor Min of Jin, Hu, wife of the clerk Ren Qiao of Xincai county, aged twenty-five, gave birth to two daughters facing each other, their bellies and hearts joined; from the chest up and from the navel down, each was separate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, Hu, wife of the clerk Ren Qiao of Xincai county, aged twenty-five, gave birth to two daughters facing each other, their bellies and hearts joined; from the chest up and from the navel down, each was separate.
